verses.1:1: I indeed produced the first account, Theophilus, concerning all the things that Jesus began to do and to teach,
verses.1:2: up to the day on which, giving commands through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom He chose, He was taken up.
verses.1:3: To them He also showed Himself alive after His suffering with many proofs, appearing to them throughout forty days and speaking concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.1:4: And while eating with them, He commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, "which you heard," He said, "through My mouth;
verses.1:5: because John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days after this."
verses.1:6: Therefore those who had gathered together were questioning Him, saying, "Lord, will You restore the kingdom to Israel at this time?"
verses.1:7: But He said to them, "It is not yours to know the times or moments that the Father has set in His own authority;
verses.1:8: but you will receive the power of the Holy Spirit coming upon you, and you will be witnesses for Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and all the way to the farthest point of the earth."
verses.1:9: And when He had said these things, as they were watching, He was lifted up, and a cloud took Him away from their eyes.
verses.1:10: And as they were gazing intently at Him going into heaven, look, two men stood beside them in white garments,
verses.1:11: who also said, "Men of Galilee, why are you standing looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will thus come, just as you saw Him going into heaven."
verses.1:12: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain that is called Olivet, which is close to Jerusalem, a Sabbath's journey away.
verses.1:13: And when they had entered into the upper room, they went up to where Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James were staying.
verses.1:14: All of these were continuing steadfastly, of one mind, in prayer with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and His brothers.
verses.1:15: In those days, standing up in the midst of the brothers, Peter said (now the crowd of people together was about one hundred twenty):
verses.1:16: "Men, brothers, it is necessary for the Scripture to be fulfilled that the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who was the guide of those who seized Jesus.
verses.1:17: He had been counted among us and obtained the allotted share of this ministry."
verses.1:18: (And this man indeed took possession of a field from the wages of iniquity, and being hanged, he burst open in the middle, and all his entrails poured out.
verses.1:19: And it became known to all those living in Jerusalem, so that in their language that field was called Hakeldama, that is, Field of Blood.)
verses.1:20: "For it is written in the book of Psalms: 'Let their dwelling become desolate, and let there be no one who dwells in it; and let another receive his office.'
verses.1:21: Therefore it is necessary that, from these men who have gathered with us throughout all the time in which the Lord Jesus went in and went out among us,
verses.1:22: beginning from the baptism of John up to the day on which He was taken up from us, one of these become a witness with us of His resurrection."
verses.1:23: And they presented two: Joseph, who was called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus; and Matthias.
verses.1:24: And praying, they said, "You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two You have chosen
verses.1:25: to receive the place of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas turned aside so that he might depart to his own place."
verses.1:26: And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.
verses.2:1: And when the days of Pentecost were being fulfilled, they were all together in the same place;
verses.2:2: and suddenly a sound came from heaven, as of a violent wind approaching, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
verses.2:3: And divided tongues, as of fire, appeared to them, and it sat on each one of them;
verses.2:4: and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak in various tongues, just as the Holy Spirit was giving them to speak out.
verses.2:5: Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation that is under heaven.
verses.2:6: And when this sound occurred, the crowd came together and was confused in mind, because each one was hearing them speaking in his own tongue.
verses.2:7: And they were all astounded and marveled, saying, "Look, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
verses.2:8: And how have we each heard our own tongue in which we were born?
verses.2:9: Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and those who live in Mesopotamia, Judea, and Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
verses.2:10: Phrygia, and Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, and visitors from Rome,
verses.2:11: Jews also, and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs: we have heard them speaking in our tongues the great deeds of God."
verses.2:12: And they were all astounded and marveled to one another, saying, "What can this mean?"
verses.2:13: But others, mocking, were saying, "These men are full of new wine."
verses.2:14: But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and spoke to them, "Jewish men, and all of you who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and receive my words with your ears.
verses.2:15: For these men are not drunk, as you assume, since it is the third hour of the day;
verses.2:16: but this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
verses.2:17: 'And it will be in the last days,' says the Lord, 'I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
verses.2:18: And indeed, on My male servants and on My female servants in those days I will pour out of My Spirit, and they will prophesy;
verses.2:19: and I will give wonders in heaven above, and signs on the earth below: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke;
verses.2:20: the sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes.
verses.2:21: And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
verses.2:22: Men of Israel, listen to these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man approved by God among you by mighty works, and wonders, and signs, which God performed through Him in your midst, just as you also know;
verses.2:23: Him, handed over by the determined plan and foreknowledge of God, you afflicted through the hands of wicked men and put to death;
verses.2:24: whom God raised up, having loosed the pains of the underworld, because it was impossible for Him to be held by it.
verses.2:25: For David says concerning Him, 'I kept seeing the Lord in My sight always, because He is at My right hand, so that I may not be shaken;
verses.2:26: for this reason My heart was glad, and My tongue exulted; moreover, My flesh also will rest in hope,
verses.2:27: because You will not abandon My soul in the underworld, nor will You allow Your Holy One to see decay.
verses.2:28: You have made known to Me the ways of life; and You will fill Me with gladness with Your face.'
verses.2:29: Men, brothers, may I be permitted to speak boldly to you concerning the patriarch David, that he died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this present day.
verses.2:30: Therefore, since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath that one from the fruit of his loins would sit on his throne,
verses.2:31: foreseeing this, he spoke concerning the resurrection of Christ, that He was neither abandoned in the underworld, nor did His flesh see decay.
verses.2:32: This Jesus God raised up, of whom all of us are witnesses.
verses.2:33: Therefore, having been exalted by the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Holy Spirit from the Father, He has poured out this One, whom you see and hear.
verses.2:34: For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself said, 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand,
verses.2:35: until I set Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.'
verses.2:36: Therefore, let all the house of Israel know most certainly that God has made Him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified."
verses.2:37: Now when they heard these things, they were pierced in heart, and said to Peter and to the rest of the apostles, "What shall we do, men, brothers?"
verses.2:38: But Peter said to them, "Repent, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
verses.2:39: For the promise is for you, and for your children, and for all who are far away, as many as the Lord our God will call."
verses.2:40: With very many other words also he testified and was exhorting them, saying, "Be saved from this perverse generation."
verses.2:41: Therefore, those who received his word were baptized, and about three thousand souls were added on that day.
verses.2:42: And they were persevering in the teaching of the apostles, and in the communion of the breaking of bread, and in prayers.
verses.2:43: And fear was coming upon every soul; many wonders and signs also were being done through the apostles in Jerusalem, and there was great dread among all of them.
verses.2:44: Also all who believed were together and had all things in common.
verses.2:45: They were selling possessions and goods, and were dividing them to all, just as each one had need.
verses.2:46: Daily also, continuing steadfastly with one mind in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they were taking food with exultation and simplicity of heart,
verses.2:47: praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord was daily increasing together those who were being saved.
verses.3:1: Now Peter and John were going up into the temple at the ninth hour of prayer.
verses.3:2: And a certain man who was lame from his mother's womb was being carried; they placed him daily at the gate of the temple that is called Beautiful, so that he might ask for alms from those entering the temple.
verses.3:3: When he saw Peter and John beginning to enter the temple, he asked to receive alms.
verses.3:4: Now looking intently at him, Peter, with John, said, "Look at us."
verses.3:5: And he paid close attention to them, hoping to receive something from them.
verses.3:6: But Peter said, "Silver and gold I do not have; yet what I have, this I give to you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise and walk."
verses.3:7: And taking hold of his right hand, he lifted him up, and at once his feet and soles were made firm.
verses.3:8: And leaping up, he stood and began walking; and he entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
verses.3:9: And all the people saw him walking and praising God.
verses.3:10: And they recognized him, that he was the very one who sat for alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple; and they were filled with astonishment and amazement at what had happened to him.
verses.3:11: Now while he was holding onto Peter and John, all the people ran to them at the portico that is called Solomon's, astonished.
verses.3:12: But when Peter saw this, he answered the people, "Men of Israel, why do you marvel at this, or why do you look intently at us, as if by our own power or authority we had made this man walk?
verses.3:13: The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His Son Jesus, whom you indeed handed over and denied before the face of Pilate, when he had decided that He should be released.
verses.3:14: But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a man who was a murderer to be granted to you;
verses.3:15: yet you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.
verses.3:16: And by faith in His name, His name has strengthened this man whom you have seen and know; and the faith that is through Him has given this complete health in the sight of all of you.
verses.3:17: And now, brothers, I know that you acted through ignorance, just as your rulers also did.
verses.3:18: But God has fulfilled in this way the things He foretold through the mouth of all the prophets, that His Christ would suffer.
verses.3:19: Repent, therefore, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped out,
verses.3:20: so that when the times of refreshment come from the presence of the Lord, and He sends Him who has been preached to you, Jesus Christ,
verses.3:21: whom heaven must indeed receive until the times of the restoration of all things that God has spoken through the mouth of His holy prophets from ancient times.
verses.3:22: Moses indeed said, 'The Lord your God will raise up a prophet for you from among your brothers, like me; you shall listen to Him according to everything that He speaks to you.
verses.3:23: And it will come about that every soul that does not listen to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.'
verses.3:24: And all the prophets, from Samuel onward, who have spoken, have announced these days.
verses.3:25: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God established with our fathers, saying to Abraham, 'And in your seed all the families of the earth will be blessed.'
verses.3:26: To you first, God, raising up His Son, sent Him blessing you, so that each one may turn himself away from his wickedness."
verses.4:1: Now while they were speaking to the people, the priests and the magistrate of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
verses.4:2: being distressed because they were teaching the people and announcing in Jesus the resurrection from the dead;
verses.4:3: and they laid hands on them and placed them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
verses.4:4: Yet many of those who had heard the word believed; and the number of the men came to be five thousand.
verses.4:5: Now it came about on the next day that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem,
verses.4:6: and Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the priestly family.
verses.4:7: And setting them in the center, they questioned them, "By what power, or in what name, did you yourselves do this?"
verses.4:8: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders, listen:
verses.4:9: if we today are being examined concerning a good deed done to an infirm man, by what means this man has been made well,
verses.4:10: let it be known to all of you, and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, by Him this man stands before you well.
verses.4:11: This is the stone that was rejected by you builders, which has become the head of the corner;
verses.4:12: and salvation is not in anyone else; nor indeed is there any other name under heaven given to people in which we must be saved."
verses.4:13: Now seeing the courage of Peter and John, and having discovered that they were unlettered and ordinary men, they marveled, and they recognized them, that they had been with Jesus;
verses.4:14: and seeing also the man who had been healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.
verses.4:15: So they ordered them to withdraw outside the council, and they conferred with one another,
verses.4:16: saying, "What shall we do with these men? For indeed a sign known to all who live in Jerusalem has been done through them; it is evident, and we cannot deny it.
verses.4:17: But so that it may not spread further among the people, let us threaten them not to speak any longer in this name to any person."
verses.4:18: And summoning them, they charged them not to speak at all nor to teach in the name of Jesus.
verses.4:19: But Peter and John, answering, said to them, "Judge whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God.
verses.4:20: For we cannot keep from speaking the things we have seen and heard."
verses.4:21: And threatening them, they released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, because all were glorifying what had been done in that which had happened.
verses.4:22: For the man on whom this sign of healing had been done was more than forty years old.
verses.4:23: And having been released, they came to their own people and reported to them all that the chief priests and elders had said to them.
verses.4:24: When they heard this, with one mind they lifted up their voice to God and said, "Lord, You are the One who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them,
verses.4:25: who by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of our father David, Your servant, said, 'Why did the nations rage, and the peoples devise futile things?
verses.4:26: The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together as one against the Lord and against His Christ.'
verses.4:27: For truly in this city there gathered together against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed, Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the nations and the peoples of Israel,
verses.4:28: to do what Your hand and Your counsel decreed to take place.
verses.4:29: And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to Your servants to speak Your word with all boldness,
verses.4:30: while You stretch out Your hand for healings, and for signs and wonders to be done through the name of Your holy Son Jesus."
verses.4:31: And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.
verses.4:32: Now the multitude of those who believed had one heart and one soul; and not one said that anything of what he possessed was his own, but everything was common to them.
verses.4:33: And with great power the apostles were giving testimony to the resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord, and great grace was in all of them.
verses.4:34: For there was not anyone needy among them; for as many as were owners of fields or houses, selling them, brought the proceeds of what they were selling
verses.4:35: and placed them before the feet of the apostles; and it was distributed to each one just as each had need.
verses.4:36: Now Joseph, who was surnamed Barnabas by the apostles (which is translated, Son of Consolation), a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
verses.4:37: since he owned a field, sold it, and brought the proceeds, and placed them before the feet of the apostles.
verses.5:1: But a certain man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a field,
verses.5:2: and fraudulently withheld some of the price of the field, his wife also being aware of it; and bringing a certain part, he placed it at the feet of the apostles.
verses.5:3: Then Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan tempted your heart, that you should lie to the Holy Spirit and fraudulently withhold some of the price of the field?
verses.5:4: While it remained, did it not remain yours, and once sold, was it not in your power? Why have you placed this matter in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God."
verses.5:5: And hearing these words, Ananias fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came upon all who heard.
verses.5:6: Then the young men rose up and removed him, and carrying him out, buried him.
verses.5:7: Now there was an interval of about three hours, and his wife, not knowing what had happened, came in.
verses.5:8: And Peter said to her, "Tell me, woman, whether you sold the field for so much?" And she said, "Yes, for so much."
verses.5:9: Then Peter said to her, "Why indeed have you agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out."
verses.5:10: Immediately she fell down before his feet and breathed her last. And the young men, coming in, found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
verses.5:11: And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.
verses.5:12: Now through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were being done among the people. And they were all of one mind in the portico of Solomon.
verses.5:13: But none of the rest dared to join themselves to them, yet the people magnified them.
verses.5:14: And a multitude of men and women believing in the Lord was increasing all the more,
verses.5:15: so that they brought out the infirm into the streets and placed them on cots and pallets, in order that, as Peter came, at least his shadow might overshadow any of them and they might be freed from their infirmities.
verses.5:16: And a multitude from the cities neighboring Jerusalem also gathered together, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, all of whom were healed.
verses.5:17: Then the high priest rose up, and all who were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees), and they were filled with jealousy,
verses.5:18: and they laid hands on the apostles and placed them in public custody.
verses.5:19: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, and leading them out, said,
verses.5:20: "Go, and standing in the temple, speak to the people all the words of this life."
verses.5:21: When they had heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and were teaching. Now when the high priest and those who were with him arrived, they summoned the council and all the elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison for them to be brought.
verses.5:22: But when the officers came and, after the prison was opened, did not find them, they returned and reported,
verses.5:23: saying, "Indeed, we found the prison shut with all diligence and the guards standing before the doors, yet on opening it we found no one inside."
verses.5:24: Now when the magistrate of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were perplexed about them as to what might happen.
verses.5:25: Then someone arrived and reported to them, "Look, the men whom you placed in prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people."
verses.5:26: Then the magistrate went with the officers and brought them without force, for they feared the people, afraid that they might be stoned.
verses.5:27: And when they had brought them, they set them in the council; and the high priest questioned them,
verses.5:28: saying, "We strictly commanded you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you want to bring the blood of this man upon us."
verses.5:29: But Peter and the apostles answered and said, "It is necessary to obey God rather than men.
verses.5:30: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you put to death by hanging Him on a tree.
verses.5:31: God exalted Him by His right hand as Prince and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins;
verses.5:32: and we are witnesses of these words, as is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to all who obey Him."
verses.5:33: When they had heard these things, they were cut to the core and were planning to kill them.
verses.5:34: But a certain Pharisee in the council, named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law honored by all the people, stood up and ordered the men to be put outside for a short while,
verses.5:35: and said to them, "Men of Israel, take care for yourselves concerning these men as to what you are about to do.
verses.5:36: For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming himself to be somebody, with whom a number of men, about four hundred, agreed. He was killed, and all who believed him were scattered and reduced to nothing.
verses.5:37: After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the registration and drew the people away after him; he also perished, and all, as many as agreed with him, were dispersed.
verses.5:38: And so now I say to you, withdraw from these men and leave them alone, because if this plan or work is from men, it will be undone;
verses.5:39: but if it is from God, you will not be able to undo it, or else you may even be found fighting against God." And they agreed with him.
verses.5:40: And summoning the apostles, after beating them, they ordered them not to speak at all in the name of Jesus, and released them.
verses.5:41: So they went away rejoicing from the presence of the council, because they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the name of Jesus.
verses.5:42: And every day they did not cease in the temple and throughout the houses, teaching and proclaiming the good news of Christ Jesus.
verses.6:1: In those days, as the number of the disciples was growing, a murmuring of the Greeks arose against the Hebrews, because their widows were being slighted in the daily ministry.
verses.6:2: So the twelve, summoning the multitude of the disciples, said, "It is not right for us to forsake the word of God and serve at tables.
verses.6:3: Therefore, brothers, look carefully for seven men from among you of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this work.
verses.6:4: But we will remain devoted to prayer and to the ministry of the word."
verses.6:5: And the statement was pleasing before the whole multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte from Antioch.
verses.6:6: These they set before the presence of the apostles, and praying, they laid hands on them.
verses.6:7: And the word of the Lord was growing, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem was multiplying greatly; a large crowd of the priests was also obeying the faith.
verses.6:8: Now Stephen, full of grace and strength, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
verses.6:9: But some from the synagogue which is called that of the Freedmen, and of the Cyrenians, and of the Alexandrians, and of those who were from Cilicia and Asia, rose up disputing with Stephen,
verses.6:10: and they were not able to resist the wisdom and the Spirit who was speaking.
verses.6:11: Then they secretly put forward men to say that they had heard him speaking words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.
verses.6:12: And so they stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes; and rushing together, they seized him and brought him into the council,
verses.6:13: and they set up false witnesses who said, "This man does not cease speaking words against the holy place and the law;
verses.6:14: for we have heard him saying that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and will change the traditions that Moses handed down to us."
verses.6:15: And gazing intently at him, all who were sitting in the council saw his face as the face of an angel.
verses.7:1: Now the high priest said, "Are these matters so?"
verses.7:2: And he said, "Men, brothers and fathers, listen: The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he stayed in Haran,
verses.7:3: and said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you.'
verses.7:4: Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. And from there, after his father died, He moved him into this land in which you now live.
verses.7:5: And He did not give him an inheritance in it, not even a foot's step; but He promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his seed after him, although he had no son.
verses.7:6: Now God spoke to him, that his seed would be a resident alien in a foreign land, and they would subject them to servitude and mistreat them for four hundred years.
verses.7:7: 'And the nation that they serve, I Myself will judge,' said the Lord, 'and after these things they will come out and serve Me in this place.'
verses.7:8: And He gave him the covenant of circumcision; and so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
verses.7:9: And the patriarchs, being jealous, sold Joseph into Egypt; and God was with him,
verses.7:10: and rescued him from all his distresses, and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, king of Egypt; and he appointed him governor over Egypt and over all his household.
verses.7:11: Now a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great distress, and our fathers were finding no food.
verses.7:12: But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers the first time;
verses.7:13: and the second time Joseph was recognized by his brothers, and his family was made known to Pharaoh.
verses.7:14: Then Joseph sent and summoned his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five souls.
verses.7:15: And Jacob went down into Egypt; and he died, he and our fathers.
verses.7:16: And they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham bought for a price of silver from the sons of Hamor, the son of Shechem.
verses.7:17: Now as the time of the promise that God had declared to Abraham was approaching, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
verses.7:18: until another king arose in Egypt who did not know Joseph.
verses.7:19: This man, dealing craftily with our people, afflicted our fathers so that they would expose their infants, that they might not be kept alive.
verses.7:20: At that same time Moses was born, and he was pleasing to God; and he was nurtured for three months in his father's house.
verses.7:21: Now when he had been exposed, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nurtured him for herself as a son.
verses.7:22: And Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and in his works.
verses.7:23: Now when a period of forty years was fulfilled for him, it rose in his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.
verses.7:24: And when he saw someone suffering wrong, he defended him and executed vengeance for the one who was enduring the wrong, by striking down the Egyptian.
verses.7:25: Now he supposed that his brothers understood that God was giving them deliverance through his hand, but they did not understand.
verses.7:26: And on the following day he appeared to them as they were quarreling, and tried to reconcile them in peace, saying, 'Men, you are brothers; why are you harming one another?'
verses.7:27: But the one who was doing wrong to his neighbor pushed him away, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
verses.7:28: You do not want to kill me just as you killed the Egyptian yesterday, do you?'
verses.7:29: And Moses fled at this word and became a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
verses.7:30: And when forty years were completed, an angel appeared to him in the desert of Mount Sinai in the fire of a flame of a bush.
verses.7:31: Now Moses, seeing it, was amazed at the sight. And as he drew near to look closely, the voice of the Lord came to him, saying,
verses.7:32: 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' And Moses, trembling, did not dare to look closely.
verses.7:33: Then the Lord said to him, 'Loosen the footwear from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.
verses.7:34: Seeing, I have seen the affliction of My people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to free them. And now come, and I will send you into Egypt.'
verses.7:35: This Moses, whom they disowned, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge?' this very one God sent as ruler and redeemer, with the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
verses.7:36: This man led them out, performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the desert for forty years.
verses.7:37: This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, 'God will raise up a prophet for you from among your brothers, like me; to him you will listen.'
verses.7:38: This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, the one who received words of life to give to us.
verses.7:39: Our fathers were unwilling to obey him, but pushed him away and turned back in their hearts to Egypt,
verses.7:40: saying to Aaron, 'Make gods for us who will go before us; for as for this Moses who led us out from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
verses.7:41: And they made a calf in those days, and offered a sacrifice to the idol, and were rejoicing in the works of their hands.
verses.7:42: But God turned away and handed them over to serve the host of heaven, just as it is written in the book of the prophets: 'Did you offer Me slaughtered animals and sacrifices for forty years in the desert, house of Israel?
verses.7:43: And you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of your god Rempham, the images that you made in order to worship them; and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.'
verses.7:44: The tabernacle of the testimony was with our fathers in the desert, just as God ordained for them, speaking to Moses, that he should make it according to the pattern that he had seen.
verses.7:45: This also our fathers, having received it, brought in with Joshua into the possession of the nations whom God drove out from before the face of our fathers, until the days of David,
verses.7:46: who found favor before God and asked that he might find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.
verses.7:47: Yet Solomon built a house for Him.
verses.7:48: But the Most High does not dwell in things made by hand, as the prophet says:
verses.7:49: 'Heaven is My throne, and the earth is the footstool of My feet. What house will you build for Me?' says the Lord, 'or what is the place of My rest?
verses.7:50: Has not My hand made all these things?'
verses.7:51: Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in hearts and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; just as your fathers did, so too do you.
verses.7:52: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who announced beforehand concerning the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now been the betrayers and murderers,
verses.7:53: you who received the law by the ordinance of angels and did not keep it."
verses.7:54: Now on hearing these things, they were cut apart in their hearts, and they were gnashing their teeth at him.
verses.7:55: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, gazing intently into heaven, saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. And he said, "Look, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
verses.7:57: Then crying out with a loud voice, they covered their ears and rushed upon him with one accord.
verses.7:58: And driving him out of the city, they were stoning him; and the witnesses laid down their garments beside the feet of a young man who was called Saul.
verses.7:59: And they were stoning Stephen as he called out and said, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
verses.7:60: Then kneeling down, he cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Lord, do not charge this sin against them." And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord. Now Saul was consenting to his killing.
verses.8:1: Now on that day a great persecution arose in the church that was in Jerusalem, and all of them were scattered through the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
verses.8:2: And God-fearing men attended to Stephen and made a great lamentation over him.
verses.8:3: But Saul was laying waste to the church; entering house by house and dragging away men and women, he was handing them over into custody.
verses.8:4: So those who had been scattered traveled about, preaching the good news of the word of God.
verses.8:5: Now Philip, going down into the city of Samaria, proclaimed Christ to them.
verses.8:6: And the crowds were paying attention to the things that were being spoken by Philip, hearing with one accord and seeing the signs that he was doing.
verses.8:7: For many of those who had unclean spirits, crying out with a loud voice, came out. Moreover, many who were paralyzed and lame were cured.
verses.8:8: Therefore, there was great joy in that city.
verses.8:9: Now there was a certain man named Simon, who previously had been a sorcerer in the city, leading astray the nation of Samaria, saying that he was someone great,
verses.8:10: to whom all were listening, from the smallest to the greatest, saying, "This man is the power of God, which is called Great."
verses.8:11: And they were giving attention to him, because for a long time he had bewitched them with his sorceries.
verses.8:12: But when they had believed Philip preaching the good news about the kingdom of God, men and women were being baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
verses.8:13: Then Simon himself also believed; and when he had been baptized, he stayed close to Philip. Seeing also signs and very great acts of power taking place, he was astonished and kept marveling.
verses.8:14: Now when the apostles who were in Jerusalem had heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
verses.8:15: When they had come, they prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit.
verses.8:16: For He had not yet come upon any one of them, but they had merely been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.8:17: Then they were laying hands upon them, and they were receiving the Holy Spirit.
verses.8:18: Now when Simon had seen that the Holy Spirit was being given through the laying on of the hand of the apostles, he offered them money,
verses.8:19: saying, "Give me this authority also, so that anyone on whom I lay hands may receive the Holy Spirit." But Peter said to him:
verses.8:20: "May your money go to destruction with you, because you supposed that the gift of God could be possessed with money.
verses.8:21: You have no share or lot in this matter, for your heart is not upright before God.
verses.8:22: Therefore repent from this wickedness of yours, and pray to God, if perhaps this thought of your heart may be forgiven you.
verses.8:23: For I see that you are in the bile of bitterness and the bond of iniquity."
verses.8:24: And Simon answered and said, "Pray yourselves for me to the Lord, so that nothing of these things that you have spoken may come upon me."
verses.8:25: And they indeed, having testified and spoken the word of the Lord, were returning to Jerusalem, and they were preaching the good news to many regions of the Samaritans.
verses.8:26: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Rise and go toward the south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is deserted.
verses.8:27: And rising, he departed. And look, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a high official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasures, had come to worship in Jerusalem.
verses.8:28: And he was returning, sitting on his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.
verses.8:29: Then the Spirit said to Philip, "Approach and join yourself to this chariot."
verses.8:30: And Philip, running up, heard him reading the prophet Isaiah and said, "Do you think you understand what you are reading?"
verses.8:31: And he said, "And how can I, unless someone shows me?" And he asked Philip to come up and sit with him.
verses.8:32: Now the passage of Scripture that he was reading was this: "Like a sheep He was led to slaughter, and as a lamb before the one shearing it is without a voice, so He did not open His mouth.
verses.8:33: In humiliation His justice was taken away. Who will recount His generation? For His life will be taken away from the earth."
verses.8:34: And the eunuch, answering Philip, said, "I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this? About himself, or about some other person?"
verses.8:35: Then Philip, opening his mouth and beginning from this Scripture, preached the good news of Jesus to him.
verses.8:36: And while they were going along the road, they came to some water; and the eunuch said, "Here is water! What hinders me from being baptized?"
verses.8:38: And he ordered the chariot to stand still, and both of them went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
verses.8:39: Now when they had come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him any longer. And he went along his way rejoicing.
verses.8:40: But Philip was found in Azotus, and as he traveled through he kept preaching the good news to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
verses.9:1: Now Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, approached the high priest
verses.9:2: and requested letters from him for Damascus, to the synagogues, so that if he found any men and women of this Way, he might lead them bound to Jerusalem.
verses.9:3: And while he was journeying, it happened that he was drawing near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven shone all around him.
verses.9:4: And as he fell to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?"
verses.9:5: He said, "Who are You, Lord?" And He replied, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting; it is hard for you to kick against the goad."
verses.9:6: And the Lord said to him, "Get up and go into the city, and there you will be told what you must do."
verses.9:7: Now those men who were traveling with him stood astounded, hearing the voice indeed, yet seeing no one.
verses.9:8: Then Saul got up from the ground, and with his eyes opened, he saw nothing; and leading him by the hands, they brought him into Damascus.
verses.9:9: And he was there for three days without seeing, and he did not eat or drink.
verses.9:10: Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus by the name of Ananias; and the Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias." He answered, "Here I am, Lord."
verses.9:11: And the Lord said to him, "Get up and go into the street that is called Straight, and search in the house of Judas for one named Saul, from Tarsus; for look, he is praying.
verses.9:12: And he has seen a man named Ananias entering and laying hands on him so that he may recover his sight."
verses.9:13: Then Ananias replied, "Lord, I have heard from many concerning this man, how many evil things he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem,
verses.9:14: and here he holds authority from the chief priests to bind all who invoke Your name."
verses.9:15: But the Lord said to him, "Go, because this man is a chosen vessel for Me, to bear My name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the sons of Israel.
verses.9:16: For I Myself will show him how much he must suffer for My name."
verses.9:17: And Ananias left and entered the house, and laying hands on him, he said, "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me, Jesus, who appeared to you on the way by which you were coming, so that you may see and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
verses.9:18: And at once things like scales fell from his eyes, and he recovered his sight; and getting up, he was baptized.
verses.9:19: And when he had taken food, he was strengthened. Now he was with the disciples who were in Damascus for several days.
verses.9:20: And immediately he was preaching Jesus in the synagogues, that He is the Son of God.
verses.9:21: Now all who were listening were astounded and were saying, "Is this not the man who in Jerusalem was attacking those who invoked this name, and came here for this purpose, so that he might lead them bound to the chief priests?"
verses.9:22: But Saul kept growing much stronger and confounded the Jews who lived in Damascus, affirming that He is the Christ.
verses.9:23: Now when many days were completed, the Jews conspired together to kill him.
verses.9:24: Yet their ambush was made known to Saul. Moreover, they were also guarding the gates day and night so that they might kill him.
verses.9:25: But the disciples, taking him by night, let him out through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
verses.9:26: Now when he had arrived in Jerusalem, he was trying to join himself to the disciples, and all of them feared him, not believing that he was a disciple.
verses.9:27: But Barnabas took hold of him and led him to the apostles, and recounted to them how on the way he had seen the Lord, and that He had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had acted boldly in the name of Jesus.
verses.9:28: And he was with them, going in and going out in Jerusalem, and acting boldly in the name of the Lord.
verses.9:29: He was also speaking to the Gentiles and disputing with the Greeks, but they were seeking to kill him.
verses.9:30: When the brothers learned of this, they led him down to Caesarea and sent him away to Tarsus.
verses.9:31: Now the church throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and was being built up, walking in the fear of the Lord, and was being filled with the consolation of the Holy Spirit.
verses.9:32: Now it happened that while Peter was passing among all of them, he came down to the saints who lived in Lydda.
verses.9:33: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been lying on a cot for eight years and was paralyzed.
verses.9:34: And Peter said to him, "Aeneas, the Lord Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your own bed." And immediately he got up.
verses.9:35: And all who resided in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
verses.9:36: Now in Joppa there was a certain female disciple named Tabitha, which translated is called Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of charity that she did.
verses.9:37: Now it happened in those days that she fell ill and died. When they had washed her, they placed her in an upper room.
verses.9:38: Now since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, on hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, pleading, "Do not hesitate to come to us."
verses.9:39: So Peter got up and came with them. And when he had arrived, they led him into the upper room, and all the widows stood around him weeping and showing him the tunics and garments that Dorcas used to make for them.
verses.9:40: Then, after sending everyone outside, Peter knelt down and prayed; and turning toward the body, he said, "Tabitha, get up." And she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
verses.9:41: Then giving her his hand, he raised her up. And when he had summoned the saints and the widows, he presented her alive.
verses.9:42: Now it became known throughout the whole of Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
verses.9:43: And it happened that he stayed for many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.
verses.10:1: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort that is called Italian,
verses.10:2: devout, and fearing God with all his household, giving many charitable gifts to the people, and praying to God always.
verses.10:3: He saw clearly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in to him and saying to him, "Cornelius."
verses.10:4: And gazing intently at him, seized with fear, he said, "What is it, lord?" And he said to him, "Your prayers and your charitable gifts have ascended as a memorial in the sight of God.
verses.10:5: And now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon, who is surnamed Peter;
verses.10:6: he is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is beside the sea; he will tell you what you must do."
verses.10:7: And when the angel who was speaking to him had departed, he called two of his household servants and a soldier fearing the Lord from those who obeyed him.
verses.10:8: And when he had recounted everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.
verses.10:9: Now on the next day, while they were making their journey and approaching the city, Peter went up to the upper level to pray, about the sixth hour.
verses.10:10: And when he became hungry, he wanted to eat; but while they were making preparations, a trance fell upon him,
verses.10:11: and he saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending, like a large linen sheet, being lowered by four corners from heaven to the earth,
verses.10:12: in which were all four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and birds of the sky.
verses.10:13: And a voice came to him, "Rise, Peter; kill and eat."
verses.10:14: But Peter said, "Far from it, Lord, because I have never eaten anything common and unclean."
verses.10:15: And a voice came to him again a second time, "What God has purified, you must not call common."
verses.10:16: Now this happened three times, and immediately the vessel was taken back into heaven.
verses.10:17: And while Peter was perplexed within himself as to what the vision that he had seen might be, look, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, inquiring for the house of Simon, stood at the gate.
verses.10:18: And when they had called out, they were asking whether Simon, who is surnamed Peter, had lodging there.
verses.10:19: Now while Peter was thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him, "Look, three men are seeking you.
verses.10:20: Rise therefore, go down, and go with them, doubting nothing, because I have sent them."
verses.10:21: And Peter, going down to the men, said, "Look, I am the one whom you are seeking; what is the reason for which you have come?"
verses.10:22: And they said, "Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and fearing God, and having testimony from the entire nation of the Jews, received an answer from a holy angel to summon you into his house and to hear words from you."
verses.10:23: Bringing them in therefore, he received them as guests. And on the following day, rising up, he set out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him.
verses.10:24: And on the next day he entered Caesarea. Now Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
verses.10:25: And it happened that when Peter had entered, Cornelius came to meet him, and falling down at his feet, worshiped.
verses.10:26: But Peter lifted him up, saying, "Stand up; I myself am also a man."
verses.10:27: And speaking with him, he went inside and found many who had gathered together,
verses.10:28: and he said to them, "You know how abominable it is for a Jewish man to associate with or approach a foreigner; yet God has shown me to call no person common or unclean.
verses.10:29: For this reason I came without hesitation when summoned. I ask therefore, for what reason have you summoned me?"
verses.10:30: And Cornelius said, "Four days ago until this hour, I was praying at the ninth hour in my house, and look, a man stood before me in a bright white garment and said,
verses.10:31: 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your charitable gifts have been remembered in the sight of God.
verses.10:32: Send therefore to Joppa and summon Simon, who is surnamed Peter; he is lodging in the house of Simon the tanner beside the sea.'
verses.10:33: Immediately therefore I sent to you, and you have done well in coming. Now therefore we are all present in your sight to hear all things that have been commanded to you by the Lord."
verses.10:34: And Peter, opening his mouth, said, "In truth I have learned that God is not partial to persons;
verses.10:35: but in every nation, the one who fears Him and works righteousness is acceptable to Him.
verses.10:36: God sent the word to the sons of Israel, announcing peace through Jesus Christ (He is Lord of all).
verses.10:37: You know the word that came about throughout all Judea, for beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John preached,
verses.10:38: Jesus from Nazareth: how God anointed Him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.
verses.10:39: And we are witnesses of all things that He did in the region of the Jews and in Jerusalem, whom they killed, hanging Him on a tree.
verses.10:40: God raised Him up on the third day and granted Him to become visible,
verses.10:41: not to all the people, but to witnesses appointed beforehand by God: to us, who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
verses.10:42: And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He Himself is the One who has been appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead.
verses.10:43: To Him all the prophets bear witness that all who believe in Him receive remission of sins through His name."
verses.10:44: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were hearing the word.
verses.10:45: And the believers from the circumcision who had come with Peter were astonished, because the grace of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even upon the nations.
verses.10:46: For they were hearing them speaking in tongues and magnifying God.
verses.10:47: Then Peter answered, "Can anyone withhold water so that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we also have?"
verses.10:48: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to remain with them for some days.
verses.11:1: Now the apostles and brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles also received the word of God.
verses.11:2: And when Peter had gone up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision were disputing against him,
verses.11:3: saying, "Why did you go in to men who are uncircumcised and eat with them?"
verses.11:4: But Peter began explaining the sequence to them, saying:
verses.11:5: "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and I saw a vision in a trance: a certain vessel descending, like a large linen sheet being lowered from heaven by four corners, and it came all the way to me.
verses.11:6: Gazing intently into it, I looked closely, and I saw four-footed animals of the earth, and wild beasts, and crawling creatures, and birds of the sky.
verses.11:7: And I also heard a voice saying to me, 'Get up, Peter; kill and eat.'
verses.11:8: But I said, 'Certainly not, Lord, because nothing common or unclean has ever gone into my mouth.'
verses.11:9: But the voice answered a second time from heaven, 'What God has cleansed, you must not call common.'
verses.11:10: And this took place three times, and all things were taken back again into heaven.
verses.11:11: And look, immediately three men stood at the house in which I was, sent from Caesarea to me.
verses.11:12: And the Spirit told me to go with them, not hesitating at all. These six brothers also came with me, and we entered the man's house.
verses.11:13: And he recounted to us how he had seen an angel in his house, standing and saying to him, 'Send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter,
verses.11:14: who will speak to you words by which you will be saved, you and your entire household.'
verses.11:15: And when I had begun to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as upon us too at the beginning.
verses.11:16: And I remembered the word of the Lord, as He used to say, 'John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
verses.11:17: Therefore, if God gave to them the same grace just as to us also who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could hinder God?"
verses.11:18: Having heard these things, they fell silent and glorified God, saying, "So then, to the Gentiles too God has given repentance to life."
verses.11:19: Now those who had been scattered because of the tribulation that had occurred at the time of Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, and Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except the Jews alone.
verses.11:20: But there were some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had entered Antioch, were speaking to the Greeks also, proclaiming the Lord Jesus.
verses.11:21: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a large number of those who believed turned to the Lord.
verses.11:22: Now the report reached the ears of the church that was in Jerusalem concerning these things, and they sent Barnabas as far as Antioch.
verses.11:23: When he had arrived and seen the grace of God, he rejoiced, and he was exhorting all of them to remain in the Lord with resolve of heart,
verses.11:24: because he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a large crowd was added to the Lord.
verses.11:25: Then Barnabas departed for Tarsus to search for Saul; and when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch.
verses.11:26: And for an entire year they associated together there in the church and taught a large crowd, so that in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.
verses.11:27: Now in these days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch,
verses.11:28: and one of them, named Agabus, stood up and indicated through the Spirit that there was going to be a great famine throughout the entire world, which took place under Claudius.
verses.11:29: So each of the disciples, according to what he had, resolved to send relief to the brothers living in Judea,
verses.11:30: which they also did, sending it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
verses.12:1: Now at that same time King Herod stretched out his hands to afflict some from the church.
verses.12:2: And he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
verses.12:3: And seeing that this pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. Now those were the days of Unleavened Bread.
verses.12:4: When he had seized him, he put him into prison, handing him over to four squads of four soldiers to be guarded, intending after the Passover to bring him out to the people.
verses.12:5: And Peter indeed was being kept in prison. But prayer was being made without ceasing by the church to God for him.
verses.12:6: Now when Herod was about to bring him out, on that very night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were guarding the prison.
verses.12:7: And look, an angel of the Lord stood there, and a light shone brightly in the room; and striking Peter's side, he woke him up, saying, "Get up quickly." And the chains fell from his hands.
verses.12:8: And the angel said to him, "Fasten your belt and put on your sandals." And he did so. And he said to him, "Wrap your cloak around yourself and follow me."
verses.12:9: And going out, he followed him, and he did not know that what was happening through the angel was real, but he supposed he was seeing a vision.
verses.12:10: And passing through the first and second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads to the city, which opened for them of its own accord. And going out, they went forward along one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.
verses.12:11: And Peter, coming back to himself, said, "Now I truly know that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews."
verses.12:12: And reflecting on this, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John, who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.
verses.12:13: And as he knocked at the door of the gate, a girl named Rhoda came forward to listen.
verses.12:14: And when she recognized Peter's voice, out of joy she did not open the gate, but running inside, she reported that Peter was standing before the gate.
verses.12:15: But they said to her, "You are out of your mind." Yet she kept insisting that it was so. And they were saying, "It is his angel."
verses.12:16: But Peter continued knocking. And when they had opened it, they saw him and were astonished.
verses.12:17: Motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he recounted how the Lord had led him out of prison, and he said, "Report these things to James and to the brothers." And going out, he departed to another place.
verses.12:18: Now when day came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers over what had become of Peter.
verses.12:19: And when Herod had searched for him and not found him, after conducting an inquiry concerning the guards, he ordered them to be led away; and going down from Judea to Caesarea, he stayed there.
verses.12:20: Now he was angry with the Tyrians and Sidonians. But they came to him with one mind, and having persuaded Blastus, who was over the king's bedchamber, they were asking for peace, because their regions were fed by him.
verses.12:21: And on an appointed day, Herod, clothed in a royal robe, sat on the judgment seat and delivered an address to them.
verses.12:22: And the people were shouting out, "The voices of a god, and not of a man!"
verses.12:23: And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he had not given honor to God; and consumed by worms, he breathed his last.
verses.12:24: But the word of the Lord was growing and multiplying.
verses.12:25: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem when they had completed the service, taking along John, who was called Mark.
verses.13:1: Now there were in the church that was at Antioch prophets and teachers, among whom were Barnabas, and Simon who was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, who was a foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
verses.13:2: And while they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to them, "Set apart for Me Saul and Barnabas for the work to which I have taken them."
verses.13:3: Then, fasting and praying, and laying hands on them, they sent them away.
verses.13:4: And they indeed, sent by the Holy Spirit, departed to Seleucia; and from there they sailed to Cyprus.
verses.13:5: And when they had come to Salamis, they were preaching the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they also had John in the ministry.
verses.13:6: And when they had walked through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-Jesus,
verses.13:7: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a prudent man. This man, having summoned Barnabas and Saul, desired to hear the word of God.
verses.13:8: But Elymas the magician was resisting them (for so his name is interpreted), seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
verses.13:9: But Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looking intently at him,
verses.13:10: said, "You who are full of all deceit and all trickery, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, you do not stop subverting the straight ways of the Lord.
verses.13:11: And now, look, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time." And immediately a mist and darkness fell upon him; and going around, he was seeking someone who would give him a hand.
verses.13:12: Then the proconsul, when he had seen what had happened, believed, marveling at the teaching of the Lord.
verses.13:13: And when Paul and those who were with him had sailed from Paphos, they came to Perga of Pamphylia. But John, departing from them, returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:14: They, however, passing through Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia; and having entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day, they sat down.
verses.13:15: And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, "Men, brothers, if there is any word of exhortation among you for the people, speak."
verses.13:16: And Paul, rising up and signaling for silence with his hand, said, "Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen:
verses.13:17: The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they were sojourners in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm brought them out of it,
verses.13:18: and for a period of forty years endured their conduct in the wilderness.
verses.13:19: And destroying seven nations in the land of Canaan, He distributed their land to them by lot,
verses.13:20: after about four hundred and fifty years; and after these things He gave judges, until Samuel the prophet.
verses.13:21: And afterward they asked for a king; and God gave them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years;
verses.13:22: and when he had been removed, He raised up David for them as king; and bearing witness to him, He said, 'I have found David the son of Jesse, a man according to My heart, who will do all My desires.'
verses.13:23: From the seed of this man, according to promise, God brought forth for Israel a Savior, Jesus,
verses.13:24: with John preaching before the face of His coming a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
verses.13:25: And as John was fulfilling his course, he was saying, 'I am not the one whom you suppose me to be; but look, One is coming after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.'
verses.13:26: Men, brothers, sons of the lineage of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, to you the word of this salvation has been sent.
verses.13:27: For those who lived in Jerusalem and its rulers, being ignorant of Him and of the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them in passing judgment,
verses.13:28: and finding no ground for death in Him, they asked Pilate that they might put Him to death.
verses.13:29: And when they had completed all things that were written about Him, taking Him down from the tree, they laid Him in a tomb.
verses.13:30: But God raised Him from the dead on the third day; and He was seen for many days by those
verses.13:31: who had gone up together with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem; and until now they are His witnesses to the people.
verses.13:32: And we proclaim to you that promise which was made to our fathers:
verses.13:33: that God has fulfilled this for our children, raising up Jesus, as it is also written in the second psalm, 'You are My Son; today I have fathered You.'
verses.13:34: And as for the fact that He raised Him from the dead, no longer to return to decay, He spoke thus, 'I will give you the faithful holy things of David.'
verses.13:35: And therefore in another place He also says, 'You will not permit Your Holy One to see decay.'
verses.13:36: For David, when he had served in his own generation, fell asleep by the will of God, and was laid with his fathers, and saw decay.
verses.13:37: But He whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.
verses.13:38: Therefore let it be known to you, men, brothers, that through Him forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and from all things from which you could not be justified in the law of Moses,
verses.13:39: in Him everyone who believes is justified.
verses.13:40: See to it, therefore, that what was spoken in the prophets does not come upon you:
verses.13:41: 'Look, despisers, and marvel, and perish; for I am working a work in your days, a work which you will not believe if anyone recounts it to you.'"
verses.13:42: And as they were going out, they were asking that on the following Sabbath they would speak these words to them.
verses.13:43: And when the synagogue had been dismissed, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking, were persuading them to remain in the grace of God.
verses.13:44: And on the following Sabbath almost the whole city came together to hear the word of God.
verses.13:45: But the Jews, seeing the crowds, were filled with jealousy, and were contradicting the things that were being spoken by Paul, blaspheming.
verses.13:46: Then Paul and Barnabas resolutely said, "It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first; but since you thrust it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look, we are turning to the Gentiles.
verses.13:47: For so the Lord has commanded us, 'I have set you as a light of the Gentiles, that you may be for salvation to the end of the earth.'"
verses.13:48: And when the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and were glorifying the word of the Lord; and as many as were preordained to eternal life believed.
verses.13:49: And the word of the Lord was being spread throughout the whole region.
verses.13:50: But the Jews incited the religious and honorable women and the leading men of the city, and aroused persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their borders.
verses.13:51: But they, having shaken off the dust of their feet against them, came to Iconium.
verses.13:52: And the disciples also were being filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
verses.14:1: Now it happened in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a way that a large multitude of Jews and Greeks believed.
verses.14:2: But the Jews who were unbelieving stirred up and provoked to anger the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.
verses.14:3: Therefore they stayed for a long time, acting boldly in the Lord, who bore witness to the word of His grace, granting signs and wonders to be done through their hands.
verses.14:4: But the multitude of the city was divided; and some indeed were with the Jews, while others were with the apostles.
verses.14:5: Now when an attack arose from the Gentiles and the Jews with their rulers to mistreat and stone them,
verses.14:6: becoming aware of it, they fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and to the entire surrounding region, and there they were preaching the gospel.
verses.14:8: And a certain man was sitting in Lystra, weak in his feet, lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
verses.14:9: This man heard Paul speaking; and Paul, gazing intently at him and seeing that he had faith to be made well,
verses.14:10: said with a loud voice, "Rise upright on your feet." And he sprang up and began walking.
verses.14:11: Now when the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voice in the Lycaonian language, saying, "The gods, having become like men, have come down to us."
verses.14:12: And they were calling Barnabas Jupiter, and Paul Mercury, because he was the leader in speaking.
verses.14:13: Also the priest of Jupiter, who was before the city, bringing bulls and garlands before the gates, wanted to offer sacrifice with the people.
verses.14:14: When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, tearing their tunics, they rushed out into the crowds, shouting
verses.14:15: and saying, "Men, why are you doing these things? We also are mortals, men like you, proclaiming to you to turn from these vain things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and all things that are in them,
verses.14:16: who in past generations permitted all the nations to walk in their own ways.
verses.14:17: And indeed He did not leave Himself without witness, doing good from heaven, giving rains and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness."
verses.14:18: And saying these things, they barely restrained the crowds from sacrificing to them.
verses.14:19: But certain Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium; and having persuaded the crowds, and stoning Paul, they dragged him outside the city, thinking that he was dead.
verses.14:20: But while the disciples surrounded him, rising up, he entered the city; and on the following day he departed with Barnabas for Derbe.
verses.14:21: And when they had preached the gospel to that city and had taught many, they returned to Lystra, and Iconium, and Antioch,
verses.14:22: strengthening the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to remain in the faith, and saying that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.14:23: And when they had appointed elders for them in each church and had prayed with fastings, they commended them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
verses.14:24: And passing through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia,
verses.14:25: and speaking the word of the Lord in Perga, they went down to Attalia;
verses.14:26: and from there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work that they had completed.
verses.14:27: Now when they had arrived and gathered the church together, they reported what great things God had done with them, and that He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
verses.14:28: And they stayed for no short time with the disciples.
verses.15:1: And certain men coming down from Judea were teaching the brothers, "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."
verses.15:2: Therefore, when no small dissension had arisen for Paul and Barnabas against them, they decided that Paul and Barnabas, along with certain others from among the others, should go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem concerning this question.
verses.15:3: So they, being escorted on their way by the church, passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles, and caused great joy to all the brothers.
verses.15:4: Now when they had come to Jerusalem, they were received by the church, and by the apostles and elders, declaring what great things God had done with them.
verses.15:5: But certain ones from the sect of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying that it is necessary for them to be circumcised, and also to command them to keep the law of Moses.
verses.15:6: And the apostles and elders came together to look into this matter.
verses.15:7: Now when much debate was taking place, Peter rose up and said to them, "Men, brothers, you know that from early days God chose among us that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe.
verses.15:8: And God, who knows the hearts, bore witness, giving them the Holy Spirit, just as also to us,
verses.15:9: and made no distinction between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
verses.15:10: Now therefore, why do you test God, to place a yoke upon the necks of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
verses.15:11: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we will be saved, in the same way as they also."
verses.15:12: And the whole multitude fell silent; and they listened to Barnabas and Paul recounting what great signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
verses.15:13: And after they became silent, James answered, saying, "Men, brothers, listen to me.
verses.15:14: Simon has recounted how God first visited to take from among the Gentiles a people for His name.
verses.15:15: And with this the words of the prophets agree, just as it is written:
verses.15:16: 'After these things I will return and rebuild the tabernacle of David that has fallen, and I will rebuild its ruins and raise it up,
verses.15:17: so that the rest of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord who does these things.'
verses.15:18: Known from eternity to the Lord is His work.
verses.15:19: For this reason I judge that those who turn to God from among the Gentiles should not be troubled,
verses.15:20: but to write to them that they should abstain from the pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.
verses.15:21: For from ancient times Moses has in each city those who preach him in the synagogues, where he is read every Sabbath."
verses.15:22: Then it pleased the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas, who was called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers,
verses.15:23: writing by their hands: "The apostles and the elders, brothers, to those who are in Antioch, and Syria, and Cilicia, brothers from among the Gentiles, greetings.
verses.15:24: Since we have heard that certain ones going out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, to whom we gave no command,
verses.15:25: it pleased us, having gathered together as one, to choose men and send them to you with our most beloved Barnabas and Paul,
verses.15:26: men who have delivered up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:27: Therefore we have sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves also report the same things to you by word.
verses.15:28: For it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you than these necessary things:
verses.15:29: that you abstain from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what has been strangled, and from fornication; keeping yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell."
verses.15:30: So they, being sent off, went down to Antioch; and having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
verses.15:31: And when they had read it, they rejoiced over the consolation.
verses.15:32: Now Judas and Silas, since they themselves were also prophets, consoled the brothers with many words and strengthened them.
verses.15:33: And when some time had passed there, they were sent off with peace by the brothers to those who had sent them.
verses.15:35: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming as good news, with many others, the word of the Lord.
verses.15:36: Now after some days, Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us return and visit the brothers throughout all the cities in which we preached the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing."
verses.15:37: Now Barnabas wanted to take John also with them, who was called Mark.
verses.15:38: But Paul urged that he, as one who had departed from them out of Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work, ought not to be received.
verses.15:39: And a dissension arose, so that they separated from one another, and Barnabas indeed, taking Mark along, sailed to Cyprus.
verses.15:40: But Paul, having chosen Silas, departed, having been committed to the grace of God by the brothers.
verses.15:41: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches, commanding them to keep the precepts of the apostles and the elders.
verses.16:1: Now he arrived at Derbe and Lystra. And look, a certain disciple was there named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman, his father being a Gentile.
verses.16:2: The brothers who were in Lystra and Iconium gave a good testimony about him.
verses.16:3: Paul wanted him to set out with him, and taking him, he circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places. For everyone knew that his father was a Gentile.
verses.16:4: Now as they passed through the cities, they delivered to them the ordinances to be observed, which had been decreed by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem.
verses.16:5: And indeed the churches were being strengthened in faith, and will abound in number daily.
verses.16:6: Now passing through Phrygia and the region of Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word of God in Asia.
verses.16:7: And when they had come into Mysia, they were trying to go into Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not permit them.
verses.16:8: Now when they had passed through Mysia, they went down to Troas.
verses.16:9: And a vision was shown to Paul during the night: a certain Macedonian man was standing and pleading with him, and saying, "Crossing over into Macedonia, help us."
verses.16:10: Now when he saw the vision, we immediately sought to set out for Macedonia, having become certain that God had called us to proclaim the gospel to them.
verses.16:11: Now sailing from Troas, we came on a straight course to Samothrace, and on the following day to Neapolis,
verses.16:12: and from there to Philippi, which is the first city of a part of Macedonia, a colony. Now we were in this city for several days, conferring.
verses.16:13: And on the Sabbath day we went outside the gate beside a river, where there seemed to be prayer, and sitting down, we were speaking to the women who had gathered.
