verses.16:14: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple of the city of the Thyatirans, worshiping God, listened; and the Lord opened her heart to pay attention to the things that were being spoken by Paul.
verses.16:15: And when she had been baptized, and her household, she pleaded, saying, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, enter my house and stay." And she compelled us.
verses.16:16: Now it happened, as we were going to prayer, that a certain girl having a spirit of Python met us, who provided great gain to her masters by divining.
verses.16:17: Following after Paul and us, she kept crying out, saying, "These men are servants of God Most High, who announce to you the way of salvation."
verses.16:18: Now she kept doing this for many days. But Paul, being grieved and turning around, said to the spirit, "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to go out from her." And it went out at that same hour.
verses.16:19: Now when her masters saw that the hope of their gain had gone out, seizing Paul and Silas, they led them into the marketplace to the rulers.
verses.16:20: And presenting them to the magistrates, they said, "These men are throwing our city into confusion, since they are Jews,
verses.16:21: and they announce a custom which it is not lawful for us to accept or to practice, since we are Romans."
verses.16:22: And the crowd rushed against them, and the magistrates, having torn off their tunics, ordered them to be beaten with rods.
verses.16:23: And when they had inflicted many blows upon them, they put them into prison, commanding the keeper to guard them diligently.
verses.16:24: When he had received such a command, he put them into the inner prison and clamped their feet in the stocks.
verses.16:25: Now at midnight Paul and Silas, praying, were praising God, and those who were in custody were listening to them.
verses.16:26: Then suddenly a great earthquake occurred, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken. And at once all the doors were opened, and the chains of everyone were loosened.
verses.16:27: Now the keeper of the prison, waking up and seeing the doors of the prison open, with his sword drawn, wanted to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had fled.
verses.16:28: But Paul cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Do no harm to yourself, for all of us are here."
verses.16:29: And having asked for a light, he went inside, and trembling with fear, he fell down at the feet of Paul and Silas.
verses.16:30: And leading them outside, he said, "Sirs, what must I do so that I may be saved?"
verses.16:31: And they said, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, and your household."
verses.16:32: And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, together with all who were in his house.
verses.16:33: And taking them at that hour of the night, he washed their wounds; and he himself was baptized, and all his household at once.
verses.16:34: And when he had led them into his house, he set a table before them and rejoiced with all his household, believing in God.
verses.16:35: And when day had come, the magistrates sent the lictors, saying, "Release those men."
verses.16:36: Now the keeper of the prison reported these words to Paul: "The magistrates have sent word that you be released; now therefore, come out and go in peace."
verses.16:37: But Paul said to them, "After beating us publicly, uncondemned Roman men, they put us into prison, and now are they casting us out secretly? Not so; rather, let them come
verses.16:38: and cast us out themselves." Now the lictors reported these words to the magistrates. And they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans.
verses.16:39: And coming, they pleaded with them, and leading them out, they asked them to depart from the city.
verses.16:40: Now going out of the prison, they went into Lydia's house; and having seen the brothers, they comforted them and set out.
verses.17:1: Now when they had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
verses.17:2: And according to custom, Paul went in to them, and for three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
verses.17:3: opening up and setting forth that it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise again from the dead, and that "This is Jesus Christ, whom I proclaim to you."
verses.17:4: And some of them believed and were joined to Paul and Silas, as well as a great multitude of the worshipers and Gentiles, and not a few noble women.
verses.17:5: But the Jews, being jealous, took some wicked men from the common crowd, and having formed a mob, they stirred up the city; and taking a stand at the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.
verses.17:6: And when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some brothers to the rulers of the city, shouting, "These men who stir up the city have come here too,
verses.17:7: whom Jason has received; and all of these act against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."
verses.17:8: And they stirred up the populace and the rulers of the city as they heard these things.
verses.17:9: And having received security from Jason and from the rest, they released them.
verses.17:10: But the brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea. And when they arrived, they went into the synagogue of the Jews.
verses.17:11: Now these were more noble than those who are in Thessalonica; they received the word with complete eagerness, searching the Scriptures every day to see if these things were so.
verses.17:12: And indeed many of them believed, as well as distinguished Gentile women, and not a few men.
verses.17:13: But when the Jews in Thessalonica learned that the word of God had been preached by Paul in Berea as well, they came there also, agitating and troubling the multitude.
verses.17:14: And immediately then the brothers sent Paul away to go as far as the sea; but Silas and Timothy remained there.
verses.17:15: Now those who were escorting Paul brought him all the way to Athens; and having received a command from him for Silas and Timothy that they should come to him as quickly as possible, they departed.
verses.17:16: Now while Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was provoked within him, seeing the city given over to idolatry.
verses.17:17: Therefore he debated in the synagogue with the Jews and the worshipers, and in the marketplace every day with those who were present.
verses.17:18: Now some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers were conversing with him, and some were saying, "What does this sower of words want to say?" Others, however, said, "He seems to be a proclaimer of new divinities," because he was proclaiming Jesus and the resurrection to them.
verses.17:19: And taking hold of him, they led him to the Areopagus, saying, "May we know what this new teaching is that is spoken by you?
verses.17:20: For you are bringing certain new things to our ears; we therefore want to know what these things mean."
verses.17:21: (Now all the Athenians and the foreign visitors devoted their time to nothing else except either to tell or to hear something new.)
verses.17:22: Then Paul, standing in the middle of the Areopagus, said, "Men of Athens, I see that in all respects you are, as it were, quite superstitious.
verses.17:23: For as I passed by and looked at your idols, I also found an altar on which was written, 'To an Unknown God.' What you therefore worship without knowing, this I proclaim to you.
verses.17:24: The God who made the world and all things that are in it, since He is the Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made by hand,
verses.17:25: nor is He worshiped by human hands as needing anything, since He Himself gives to all life, and breath, and all things;
verses.17:26: and He made from one every race of mankind to dwell upon the entire face of the earth, determining the appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
verses.17:27: to seek God, if perhaps they might grope for Him or find Him, although He is not far from each one of us.
verses.17:28: For in Him we live, and move, and exist, as also some of your poets have said, 'For we too are His offspring.'
verses.17:29: Therefore, since we are the offspring of God, we should not suppose that the Divine is like gold, or silver, or stone, a carving of the skill and thought of man.
verses.17:30: And indeed, overlooking the times of this ignorance, God now proclaims to mankind that everyone everywhere should repent,
verses.17:31: because He has appointed a day on which He is going to judge the world in equity through a man whom He has appointed, giving assurance to all by raising Him from the dead."
verses.17:32: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some indeed mocked, while others said, "We will hear you about this again."
verses.17:33: So Paul went out from their midst.
verses.17:34: Certain men, however, attaching themselves to him, believed; among whom were also Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
verses.18:1: After these things, departing from Athens, he came to Corinth.
verses.18:2: And finding a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife (because Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome), he went to them.
verses.18:3: And because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked. (Now they were of the tentmaking trade.)
verses.18:4: And he debated in the synagogue every Sabbath, introducing the name of the Lord Jesus, and was persuading Jews and Greeks.
verses.18:5: Now when Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul applied himself intently to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
verses.18:6: But as they contradicted and blasphemed, shaking out his garments, he said to them, "Your blood be on your head; I am clean; from now on I will go to the Gentiles."
verses.18:7: And moving from there, he entered the house of a certain man named Titus Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house adjoined the synagogue.
verses.18:8: Now Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord together with his entire household; and many of the Corinthians, as they heard, believed and were baptized.
verses.18:9: And the Lord said to Paul at night through a vision, "Do not be afraid, but speak, and do not stay silent,
verses.18:10: because I am with you, and no one will set upon you to harm you, for I have many people in this city."
verses.18:11: And he stayed there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
verses.18:12: Now while Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up with one accord against Paul and brought him to the tribunal,
verses.18:13: saying, "This man is persuading people to worship God contrary to the law."
verses.18:14: But just as Paul was beginning to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, "If indeed it were some wrongdoing or a heinous crime, Jewish men, I would rightly bear with you.
verses.18:15: But if they are questions about a word, and names, and your law, see to it yourselves; I do not wish to be a judge of these matters."
verses.18:16: And he drove them from the tribunal.
verses.18:17: Then they all seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and were beating him in front of the tribunal; and none of those things was of concern to Gallio.
verses.18:18: Paul, however, after staying many days longer, took leave of the brothers and sailed for Syria (and Priscilla and Aquila were with him), having shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
verses.18:19: And he arrived at Ephesus and left them there. But he himself entered the synagogue and debated with the Jews.
verses.18:20: And when they asked him to stay for a longer time, he did not consent,
verses.18:21: but taking leave and saying, "I will return to you again, God willing," he departed from Ephesus.
verses.18:22: And going down to Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church, and went down to Antioch.
verses.18:23: And after spending some time there, he departed, traveling in order through the Galatian region and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
verses.18:24: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, an eloquent man, arrived at Ephesus, being mighty in the Scriptures.
verses.18:25: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John.
verses.18:26: This man, therefore, began to act boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of the Lord more accurately.
verses.18:27: Now when he wanted to go to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to receive him. And when he had arrived, he contributed much to those who had believed;
verses.18:28: for he vigorously refuted the Jews in public, showing through the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
verses.19:1: Now it happened, while Apollos was at Corinth, that Paul, having traveled through the upper regions, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
verses.19:2: And he said to them, "Have you received the Holy Spirit upon believing?" But they said to him, "No, we have not even heard if there is a Holy Spirit."
verses.19:3: He, however, said, "In what, then, were you baptized?" And they said, "In John's baptism."
verses.19:4: Now Paul said, "John baptized the people with a baptism of repentance, saying that they should believe in Him who was to come after him, that is, in Jesus."
verses.19:5: Having heard these things, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.19:6: And when Paul had laid hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and prophesying.
verses.19:7: Now the men were about twelve in all.
verses.19:8: And having entered the synagogue, he spoke with boldness for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.19:9: But when some became hardened and did not believe, speaking evil of the way of the Lord before the multitude, he departed from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of a certain tyrant.
verses.19:10: Now this took place for two years, so that all who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord, Jews as well as Gentiles.
verses.19:11: And God was working no ordinary miracles through the hand of Paul,
verses.19:12: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons were carried from his body onto the sick, and the sicknesses departed from them, and the wicked spirits went out.
verses.19:13: Now some of the wandering Jewish exorcists also tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, "I charge you under oath by Jesus, whom Paul preaches."
verses.19:14: Now there were certain Jews, seven sons of Sceva, a chief priest, who were doing this.
verses.19:15: But the wicked spirit answered and said to them, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know of; but who are you?"
verses.19:16: And the man in whom there was a most evil demon, leaping upon them and overpowering both of them, prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
verses.19:17: Now this became known to all the Jews and Gentiles who lived in Ephesus, and fear fell upon all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.
verses.19:18: And many of the believers were coming, confessing and declaring their deeds.
verses.19:19: And many of those who had pursued magical arts brought books together and burned them before everyone; and having calculated their prices, they found the sum of money to be fifty thousand denarii.
verses.19:20: So powerfully was the word of God growing and being strengthened.
verses.19:21: Now when these things were completed, Paul resolved in the Spirit, after passing through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, "After I have been there, I must see Rome also."
verses.19:22: And sending to Macedonia two of those who ministered to him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself remained in Asia for a time.
verses.19:23: Now at that time no small disturbance occurred concerning the way of the Lord.
verses.19:24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith making silver shrines of Diana, was bringing no small profit to the craftsmen.
verses.19:25: Summoning them, together with those who were workers of this sort, he said, "Men, you know that from this craft we have our income,
verses.19:26: and you see and hear that not only at Ephesus, but throughout almost all of Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away a large crowd, saying, 'Those that are made by hands are not gods.'
verses.19:27: And not only will this business of ours be in danger of coming into discredit, but also the temple of the great Diana will be reckoned as nothing, and even the majesty of her whom all Asia and the world worship will begin to be destroyed."
verses.19:28: Having heard these things, they were filled with anger and cried out, saying, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"
verses.19:29: And the city was filled with confusion, and with one mind they rushed into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, companions of Paul.
verses.19:30: Now when Paul wanted to go in among the people, the disciples did not permit it.
verses.19:31: And some also of the rulers of Asia, who were his friends, sent to him, asking him not to venture into the theater.
verses.19:32: Meanwhile, some were shouting one thing and some another. For the assembly was in confusion, and the majority did not know for what reason they had come together.
verses.19:33: Now they drew Alexander out of the crowd, with the Jews pushing him forward. And Alexander, having requested silence with his hand, wanted to give an account to the people.
verses.19:34: When they recognized that he was a Jew, one voice arose from them all, shouting for about two hours, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"
verses.19:35: And when the city clerk had calmed the crowds, he said, "Men of Ephesus, who indeed among people does not know that the city of the Ephesians is the worshiper of the great Diana and of the offspring of Jupiter?
verses.19:36: Since, therefore, these things cannot be contradicted, you ought to be calm and do nothing rashly.
verses.19:37: For you have brought these men here, who are neither sacrilegious nor blaspheming your goddess.
verses.19:38: So if Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a case against anyone, court sessions are held and there are proconsuls; let them accuse one another.
verses.19:39: But if you seek anything regarding another matter, it can be settled in the lawful assembly.
verses.19:40: For we are even in danger of being accused of today's sedition, since there is no one guilty concerning whom we can give an account of this gathering." And when he had said these things, he dismissed the assembly.
verses.20:1: Now after the uproar ceased, Paul, having summoned the disciples and exhorted them, said farewell and departed to go into Macedonia.
verses.20:2: And when he had traveled through those regions and had exhorted them with many words, he came to Greece,
verses.20:3: where, when he had spent three months, a plot was laid against him by the Jews as he was about to sail to Syria; and he formed a plan to return through Macedonia.
verses.20:4: Now Sopater, son of Pyrrhus, a Berean, accompanied him; and from the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and from Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
verses.20:5: These men, having gone on ahead, waited for us at Troas;
verses.20:6: but we sailed from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed for seven days.
verses.20:7: Now on the first day of the week, when we had come together to break bread, Paul was discoursing with them, about to depart on the next day, and he prolonged his speech until midnight.
verses.20:8: And there were numerous lamps in the upper room where we were assembled.
verses.20:9: Now a certain young man named Eutychus, sitting on the windowsill, was sinking into a heavy sleep as Paul discoursed at length; carried away by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.
verses.20:10: When Paul had gone down to him, he lay down upon him, and embracing him, he said, "Do not be disturbed, for his life is in him."
verses.20:11: Then going up, and breaking bread and eating, and having spoken at length until daylight, he thus departed.
verses.20:12: And they brought the boy alive, and they were comforted in no small measure.
verses.20:13: Now we, embarking on the ship, sailed to Assos, intending to take Paul aboard from there; for he had so arranged, as he himself was going to travel by land.
verses.20:14: And when he had met us at Assos, having taken him aboard, we came to Mitylene.
verses.20:15: And sailing from there, on the following day we came opposite Chios, and on the next day we put in at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.
verses.20:16: For Paul had resolved to sail past Ephesus, so that no delay might occur for him in Asia. For he was hurrying, if it were possible for him, to spend the day of Pentecost in Jerusalem.
verses.20:17: Now from Miletus, sending to Ephesus, he summoned the elders of the church.
verses.20:18: When they had come to him and were together, he said to them, "You know, from the first day on which I entered Asia, in what manner I was with you throughout the whole time,
verses.20:19: serving the Lord with all humility and tears and trials that came upon me from the plots of the Jews;
verses.20:20: how I withheld nothing of what was beneficial, proclaiming it to you and teaching you publicly and house by house,
verses.20:21: testifying to Jews as well as Gentiles repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.20:22: And now, look, bound in spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what things will happen to me in it,
verses.20:23: except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me throughout all the cities, saying that chains and afflictions await me in Jerusalem.
verses.20:24: Yet I fear none of these things, nor do I regard my life as more precious than myself, provided only that I finish my course and the ministry of the word that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God.
verses.20:25: And now, look, I know that you will see my face no longer, all of you among whom I passed preaching the kingdom of God.
verses.20:26: Therefore I solemnly testify to you on this day that I am clean from the blood of all.
verses.20:27: For I did not shrink back from proclaiming the entire counsel of God to you.
verses.20:28: Pay attention to yourselves and to the entire flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as overseers to govern the church of God, which He acquired with His own blood.
verses.20:29: I know that ravenous wolves will enter among you after my departure, not sparing the flock.
verses.20:30: And from among yourselves men will rise up speaking perverse things, in order to lead the disciples away after themselves.
verses.20:31: For this reason, stay alert, keeping in mind that for three years, night and day, I did not cease admonishing each one of you with tears.
verses.20:32: And now I entrust you to God and to the word of His grace, who is able to edify and to give an inheritance among all who have been sanctified.
verses.20:33: I have coveted no one's silver and gold, or clothing, just as
verses.20:34: you yourselves know; for these hands provided for the things that I needed and for those who are with me.
verses.20:35: I have shown you all things: that by laboring in this way it is necessary to support the weak and to remember the word of the Lord Jesus, for He Himself said, 'It is more blessed to give rather than to receive.'"
verses.20:36: And after he had said these things, having knelt down, he prayed with all of them.
verses.20:37: Now a great weeping arose among all of them, and falling upon Paul's neck, they kept kissing him,
verses.20:38: grieving most of all at the word he had spoken, that they would no longer see his face. And they escorted him to the ship.
verses.21:1: Now when it came about that we set sail, after being torn away from them, we came on a straight course to Cos, and on the following day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
verses.21:2: And when we had found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, going aboard, we set sail.
verses.21:3: Now when we had come into view of Cyprus, leaving it on the left, we sailed to Syria and came to Tyre, for there the ship was going to unload the cargo.
verses.21:4: And having found the disciples, we stayed there seven days; and they were telling Paul through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.21:5: And when the days were completed, we set out and went on, while all of them, together with their wives and children, escorted us all the way outside the city; and kneeling down on the shore, we prayed.
verses.21:6: And when we had said farewell to one another, we boarded the ship, while they returned to their own homes.
verses.21:7: And we, having completed the voyage from Tyre, came down to Ptolemais; and having greeted the brothers, we stayed one day with them.
verses.21:8: And setting out on the next day, we came to Caesarea. And entering the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we stayed with him.
verses.21:9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
verses.21:10: And while we were staying for several days, a certain prophet named Agabus arrived from Judea.
verses.21:11: When he had come to us, he took Paul's belt, and binding his own feet and hands, he said, "This is what the Holy Spirit says: 'The man whose belt this is, the Jews in Jerusalem will bind in this way and hand over into the hands of the Gentiles.'"
verses.21:12: When we had heard this, both we and those who were of that place kept pleading with him not to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.21:13: Then Paul answered and said, "What are you doing, weeping and afflicting my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the sake of the name of the Lord Jesus."
verses.21:14: And when we could not persuade him, we fell silent, saying, "May the Lord's will be done."
verses.21:15: Now after these days, having made preparations, we were going up to Jerusalem.
verses.21:16: And some of the disciples from Caesarea also came with us, bringing with them a certain Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to lodge.
verses.21:17: And when we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
verses.21:18: Now on the following day Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders were assembled.
verses.21:19: When he had greeted them, he related one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
verses.21:20: And when they had heard it, they were magnifying God, and they said to him, "You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.
verses.21:21: Now they have heard about you that you teach the Jews who are among the Gentiles a departure from Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their sons, nor to walk according to custom.
verses.21:22: What is it, then? Certainly the multitude must assemble, for they will hear that you have arrived.
verses.21:23: Therefore do this that we tell you. We have four men who have a vow upon themselves.
verses.21:24: Taking these men, sanctify yourself with them and pay expenses for them so that they may shave their heads; and all will know that the things they have heard about you are false, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.
verses.21:25: Now concerning those from among the Gentiles who have believed, we have written, judging that they should abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what has been strangled, and from fornication."
verses.21:26: Then Paul, taking the men, on the next day was purified with them and entered the temple, announcing the completion of the days of purification, until an offering should be offered for each one of them.
verses.21:27: Now while the seven days were coming to completion, the Jews who were from Asia, when they had seen him in the temple, stirred up all the people and laid hands on him, shouting,
verses.21:28: "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who, teaching everyone everywhere against the people and the law and this place, has furthermore also brought Gentiles into the temple and defiled this holy place."
verses.21:29: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they supposed Paul had brought into the temple.
verses.21:30: And the whole city was thrown into commotion, and a rushing together of the people took place. And seizing Paul, they were dragging him outside the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
verses.21:31: Now while they were seeking to kill him, it was reported to the tribune of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion.
verses.21:32: He at once, taking soldiers and centurions, ran down to them. And when they had seen the tribune and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
verses.21:33: Then the tribune approached, seized him, and ordered him to be bound with two chains; and he was inquiring who he was and what he had done.
verses.21:34: But some in the crowd were shouting one thing and some another. And when he could not learn anything certain because of the uproar, he ordered him to be led into the barracks.
verses.21:35: And when he had come to the steps, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the people.
verses.21:36: For the multitude of the people was following, shouting, "Away with him!"
verses.21:37: And when Paul had begun to be led into the barracks, he said to the tribune, "Is it permitted for me to say something to you?" And he said, "Do you know Greek?
verses.21:38: Are you not the Egyptian who before these days stirred up an uproar and led out into the desert four thousand men of the assassins?"
verses.21:39: And Paul said to him, "I am indeed a Jewish man from Tarsus of Cilicia, a citizen of no obscure city. Now I ask you, permit me to speak to the people."
verses.21:40: And when he had permitted it, Paul, standing on the steps, motioned with his hand to the people; and when a great silence had come about, he addressed them in the Hebrew language, saying:
verses.22:1: "Men, brothers, and fathers, hear the defense that I now give to you."
verses.22:2: Now when they had heard that he was speaking to them in the Hebrew language, they kept silence all the more.
verses.22:3: And he said, "I am a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, yet brought up in this city, educated at the feet of Gamaliel according to the truth of the ancestral law, zealous for the law, just as you all are today;
verses.22:4: who persecuted this Way even to death, binding and handing over into prisons men and women,
verses.22:5: as the high priest bears witness for me, and all the elders; from whom also receiving letters to the brothers, I was proceeding to Damascus so that I might bring those who were bound from there to Jerusalem to be punished.
verses.22:6: Now it came about that as I was going and approaching Damascus at midday, suddenly an abundant light from heaven flashed around me;
verses.22:7: and falling to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'
verses.22:8: And I answered, 'Who are You, Lord?' And He said to me, 'I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.'
verses.22:9: And those who were with me indeed saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of Him who was speaking with me.
verses.22:10: And I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?' And the Lord said to me, 'Get up and go to Damascus, and there you will be told about all the things that you must do.'
verses.22:11: And since I could not see because of the brightness of that light, being led by the hand by my companions, I came to Damascus.
verses.22:12: Now a certain Ananias, a man according to the law, attested by all the Jews living there,
verses.22:13: coming to me and standing beside me, said to me, 'Brother Saul, look up.' And in that same hour I looked up at him.
verses.22:14: And he said, 'The God of our fathers has preordained you to know His will, and to see the Just One, and to hear a voice from His mouth;
verses.22:15: because you will be His witness to all people of the things that you have seen and heard.
verses.22:16: And now why do you delay? Rise up and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling upon His name.'
verses.22:17: Now it came about, when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance
verses.22:18: and saw Him saying to me, 'Hurry, and go out quickly from Jerusalem, because they will not accept your testimony about Me.'
verses.22:19: And I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that I was locking up in prison and beating throughout the synagogues those who believed in You;
verses.22:20: and when the blood of Stephen Your witness was being shed, I myself was standing by and consenting, and guarding the garments of those who were killing him.'
verses.22:21: And He said to me, 'Go, because I will send you far away to the nations.'"
verses.22:22: Now they were listening to him up to this word, and they raised their voice, saying, "Remove such a man from the earth, for it is not right for him to live!"
verses.22:23: And as they were shouting loudly, and throwing off their garments, and tossing dust into the air,
verses.22:24: the tribune ordered him to be led into the barracks, and to be beaten with whips and tortured, so that he might know for what reason they were shouting at him in this way.
verses.22:25: And when they had bound him tightly with leather straps, Paul said to the centurion standing beside him, "Is it lawful for you to flog a man who is a Roman and uncondemned?"
verses.22:26: Hearing this, the centurion approached the tribune and reported to him, saying, "What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman citizen."
verses.22:27: And the tribune approached and said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?" And he said, "Yes."
verses.22:28: And the tribune answered, "With a large sum I acquired this citizenship." And Paul said, "But I was even born one."
verses.22:29: Immediately, therefore, those who were about to torture him withdrew from him. The tribune also became afraid after he learned that he was a Roman citizen, and because he had bound him.
verses.22:30: Now on the next day, wishing to know more accurately for what reason he was being accused by the Jews, he unbound him and ordered the priests and the whole council to assemble; and bringing Paul out, he set him among them.
verses.23:1: Now looking intently at the council, Paul said, "Men, brothers, I have conducted myself with all good conscience before God up to this very day."
verses.23:2: And the high priest Ananias commanded those standing beside him to strike his mouth.
verses.23:3: Then Paul said to him, "God will strike you, whitewashed wall. And you sit judging me according to the law, and contrary to the law you order me to be struck?"
verses.23:4: And those who were standing nearby said, "You are cursing the high priest of God."
verses.23:5: And Paul said, "I did not know, brothers, that he is the high priest. For it is written, 'You shall not curse the ruler of your people.'"
verses.23:6: Now Paul, knowing that one part was Sadducees and the other Pharisees, cried out in the council, "Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees; concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged."
verses.23:7: And when he had said these things, a dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was split apart.
verses.23:8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, but the Pharisees confess both.
verses.23:9: Then a great outcry arose. And some of the Pharisees stood up and contended, saying, "We find nothing wrong in this man; what if a spirit spoke to him, or an angel?"
verses.23:10: And when a great dissension had arisen, the tribune, fearing that Paul might be torn to pieces by them, ordered the soldiers to go down and snatch him from their midst, and to bring him into the barracks.
verses.23:11: Now on the following night, standing beside him, the Lord said, "Be steadfast; for just as you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so you must testify in Rome also."
verses.23:12: And when day came, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they killed Paul.
verses.23:13: Now there were more than forty men who had formed this conspiracy.
verses.23:14: They went to the chief priests and the elders and said, "With a curse we have bound ourselves to taste nothing until we kill Paul.
verses.23:15: Now therefore, you, together with the council, make it known to the tribune to bring him forth to you, as though you were about to ascertain something more certain concerning him. And we, before he comes near, are ready to kill him."
verses.23:16: Now when the son of Paul's sister heard of the ambush, he came and entered the barracks and reported it to Paul.
verses.23:17: Then Paul, calling one of the centurions to himself, said, "Bring this young man to the tribune, for he has something to report to him."
verses.23:18: So he took him and led him to the tribune and said, "The prisoner Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to speak to you."
verses.23:19: And the tribune, taking hold of his hand, withdrew with him privately and questioned him, "What is it that you have to report to me?"
verses.23:20: And he said, "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul forth tomorrow into the council, as though they were about to inquire into something more certain concerning him;
verses.23:21: but do not believe them; for more than forty men from among them are lying in ambush for him, who have bound themselves under a curse not to eat nor to drink until they kill him; and now they are ready, awaiting your promise."
verses.23:22: Therefore the tribune dismissed the young man, commanding him to tell no one that he had made these things known to him.
verses.23:23: And having called two centurions, he said to them, "Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, from the third hour of the night,
verses.23:24: and prepare mounts so that, placing Paul on them, they may bring him safely to Felix the governor."
verses.23:25: (For he feared that perhaps the Jews might seize him and kill him, and that he himself might afterward suffer a false accusation, as though about to accept money.)
verses.23:26: He wrote a letter containing these words: "Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix, greetings.
verses.23:27: This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them; coming upon them with the troops, I rescued him, having learned that he is a Roman.
verses.23:28: And wanting to know the charge that they were bringing against him, I brought him down into their council.
verses.23:29: I found him to be accused concerning questions of their law, but having no charge deserving of death or chains.
verses.23:30: And when it was reported to me about the ambush that they had prepared for him, I sent him to you, notifying the accusers also to speak before you. Farewell."
verses.23:31: Therefore the soldiers, taking Paul according to the command given to them, led him by night to Antipatris.
verses.23:32: And on the next day, having sent the horsemen on to go with him, they returned to the barracks.
verses.23:33: When they had come to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they presented Paul before him as well.
verses.23:34: And when he had read it and asked what province he was from, and learned that he was from Cilicia,
verses.23:35: "I will hear you," he said, "when your accusers have arrived." And he ordered him to be kept under guard in Herod's praetorium.
verses.24:1: Now after five days, the high priest Ananias came down with certain elders and a certain orator, Tertullus, and they appeared before the governor against Paul.
verses.24:2: And when Paul had been summoned, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, "Since we live in great peace through you, and many things are set right through your foresight,
verses.24:3: we accept it always and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.
verses.24:4: Yet so that I may not detain you any longer, I beg that you hear us briefly in your clemency.
verses.24:5: We have found this man to be pestilent, stirring up seditions among all the Jews throughout the whole world, and an instigator of the sedition of the sect of the Nazarenes,
verses.24:6: who even tried to violate the temple; and having seized him, we wanted to judge him according to our law,
verses.24:8: ordering his accusers to come to you; from whom you yourself, in judging, will be able to learn about all these things of which we accuse him."
verses.24:9: And the Jews also joined in, saying that these things were so.
verses.24:10: Then Paul answered (the governor nodding to him to speak), "Knowing that for many years you have been a judge over this nation, I will with good courage make my defense.
verses.24:11: For you are able to ascertain that it has been no more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem;
verses.24:12: and neither in the temple did they find me disputing with anyone or causing a crowd to gather, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city;
verses.24:13: nor can they prove to you the things concerning which they now accuse me.
verses.24:14: Yet I confess this to you, that according to the sect that they call a heresy, so I serve the Father and my God, believing all things that are written in the law and the prophets,
verses.24:15: having a hope in God, which these men themselves also await, that there will be a resurrection of the just and the unjust.
verses.24:16: In this I myself also strive to have a conscience without offense toward God and toward people always.
verses.24:17: Now after several years, I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings, and vows,
verses.24:18: in which they found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd, nor with a tumult.
verses.24:19: Yet certain Jews from Asia, who ought to be present before you and accuse me if they had anything against me;
verses.24:20: or let these men themselves say if they found any wrongdoing in me when I stood in the council,
verses.24:21: except concerning this one utterance alone that I cried out while standing among them, 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged today by you.'"
verses.24:22: Then Felix put them off, knowing most accurately about this Way, saying, "When the tribune Lysias comes down, I will hear you."
verses.24:23: And he ordered the centurion to keep him under guard, and to allow him respite, and not to forbid any of his own people to attend to him.
verses.24:24: Now after some days, Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and called for Paul, and heard from him of the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.24:25: And as he discoursed on righteousness, and chastity, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified and answered, "For the present, go; at an opportune time I will summon you."
verses.24:26: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul; for this reason he also summoned him frequently and spoke with him.
verses.24:27: Now when two years were completed, Felix received Porcius Festus as his successor. And wanting to grant a favor to the Jews, Felix left Paul a prisoner.
verses.25:1: Therefore, when Festus had come into the province, after three days he went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
verses.25:2: And the chief priests and the leading men of the Jews approached him against Paul, and they kept asking him,
verses.25:3: requesting a favor against him, that he would order him to be brought to Jerusalem, laying an ambush to kill him on the road.
verses.25:4: But Festus answered that Paul was being kept in Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart very soon.
verses.25:5: "Therefore," he said, "let those among you who hold authority go down together; if there is any offense in the man, let them accuse him."
verses.25:6: Now having stayed among them no more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat at the tribunal and ordered Paul to be brought forward.
verses.25:7: When he had been brought in, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges which they could not prove,
verses.25:8: while Paul gave his account: "Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I committed any offense."
verses.25:9: But Festus, wishing to do a favor for the Jews, answered Paul and said, "Do you wish to go up to Jerusalem and be judged there concerning these things before me?"
verses.25:10: But Paul said, "I am standing at Caesar's tribunal; there I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no wrong, as you know full well.
verses.25:11: For if I have done wrong, or have committed anything deserving of death, I do not refuse to die; but if there is nothing in the things of which these men accuse me, no one can grant me to them. I appeal to Caesar."
verses.25:12: Then Festus, after speaking with the council, answered, "Have you appealed to Caesar? To Caesar you will go."
verses.25:13: And when several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to greet Festus.
verses.25:14: And while they were staying there for many days, Festus reported to the king about Paul, saying, "There is a certain man left behind by Felix as a prisoner,
verses.25:15: about whom, when I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews approached me, requesting condemnation against him.
verses.25:16: To them I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to condemn any man before the one who is accused has his accusers present and receives an opportunity for defense to clear away the charges.
verses.25:17: Therefore, when they had assembled here without any delay, on the following day, sitting at the tribunal, I ordered the man to be brought forward.
verses.25:18: Concerning him, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of the things about which I was suspecting evil.
verses.25:19: Rather, they had certain disputes against him about their own superstition, and about a certain Jesus who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.25:20: Now I, uncertain about a dispute of this kind, asked whether he wished to go to Jerusalem and be judged there concerning these things.
verses.25:21: But when Paul appealed to be kept for the hearing of Augustus, I ordered him to be kept until I send him to Caesar."
verses.25:22: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I myself also wanted to hear the man." "Tomorrow," he said, "you will hear him."
verses.25:23: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had arrived with great pageantry and had entered the audience hall with the tribunes and the foremost men of the city, at Festus's command Paul was brought forward.
verses.25:24: And Festus said, "King Agrippa, and all the men who are present together with us, you see this man about whom the entire multitude of the Jews petitioned me in Jerusalem, demanding and shouting out that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.25:25: I indeed discovered that he had committed nothing deserving of death. However, since this man himself appealed to Augustus, I decided to send him.
verses.25:26: Concerning him I have nothing definite to write to my lord. For this reason I have brought him forth before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that once an examination has been conducted, I may have something to write.
verses.25:27: For it seems unreasonable to me to send a prisoner and not indicate the charges against him."
verses.26:1: Now Agrippa said to Paul, "You are permitted to speak for yourself." Then Paul, stretching out his hand, began to give his account:
verses.26:2: "Concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate that I am going to defend myself before you today,
verses.26:3: especially since you know all things, both the customs and the disputes that exist among the Jews; for this reason I implore you to listen to me patiently.
verses.26:4: Indeed, my life from youth, which from the beginning was among my nation in Jerusalem, all the Jews know,
verses.26:5: having known me from the beginning (if they are willing to bear witness) that according to the most certain sect of our religion I lived as a Pharisee.
verses.26:6: And now, in the hope of the promise that was made by God to our fathers, I stand subject to judgment,
verses.26:7: to which our twelve tribes, serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, king.
verses.26:8: Why is it judged incredible among you if God raises the dead?
verses.26:9: Indeed, I myself had supposed that I ought to do many opposing things against the name of Jesus the Nazarene,
verses.26:10: which I also did in Jerusalem; and many of the saints I myself shut up in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were being put to death, I delivered sentence.
verses.26:11: And throughout all the synagogues, frequently punishing them, I kept compelling them to blaspheme; and raging even more madly against them, I persecuted them even into foreign cities.
verses.26:12: In these matters, while I was going to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests,
verses.26:13: at midday on the road I saw, king, a light from heaven, surpassing the splendor of the sun, shine around me and those who were together with me.
verses.26:14: And when all of us had fallen down to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goad.'
verses.26:15: And I said, 'Who are You, Lord?' And the Lord said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.26:16: But rise up and stand on your feet; for to this purpose I have appeared to you, to appoint you as a servant and a witness of the things that you have seen and of those things in which I will appear to you,
verses.26:17: rescuing you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am now sending you,
verses.26:18: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a portion among the saints, through the faith that is in Me.'
verses.26:19: Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not unbelieving toward the heavenly vision,
verses.26:20: but to those who are in Damascus first, and in Jerusalem, and throughout the entire region of Judea, and to the Gentiles, I kept proclaiming that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
verses.26:21: For this reason the Jews seized me when I was in the temple and tried to kill me.
verses.26:22: Yet, assisted by the help of God up to this very day, I stand bearing witness to both small and great, saying nothing beyond those things which the prophets and Moses spoke would take place:
verses.26:23: whether the Christ is subject to suffering, whether, as the first from the resurrection of the dead, He is about to proclaim light to the people and to the Gentiles."
verses.26:24: While he was speaking these things and giving his account, Festus said with a loud voice, "You are mad, Paul! Much learning is turning you to madness."
verses.26:25: And Paul said, "I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.
verses.26:26: For the king knows about these things, to whom I also speak with confidence; for I think that none of these things is hidden from him. Indeed, none of these things took place in a corner.
verses.26:27: Do you believe the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you believe."
verses.26:28: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "In a small measure you are persuading me to become a Christian."
verses.26:29: And Paul said, "I pray to God that, both in a small measure and in a great one, not only you, but also all who are listening today, may become such as I also am, except for these chains."
verses.26:30: And the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and those who were sitting with them.
verses.26:31: And when they had withdrawn, they were speaking to one another, saying, "This man has done nothing deserving of death or chains."
verses.26:32: And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar."
verses.27:1: Now when it was decided that he should sail to Italy, and that Paul with the rest of the prisoners should be handed over to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort,
verses.27:2: we boarded a ship of Adramyttium and, beginning to sail around the places of Asia, weighed anchor, with Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, remaining with us.
verses.27:3: And on the following day we arrived at Sidon. And Julius, treating Paul kindly, permitted him to go to friends and take care of himself.
verses.27:4: And after we had weighed anchor from there, we sailed in the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.27:5: And sailing across the open sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Lystra, which is in Lycia.
verses.27:6: And there the centurion, finding an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy, transferred us onto it.
verses.27:7: And when we had sailed slowly for many days and had with difficulty arrived opposite Cnidus, as the wind hindered us, we sailed toward Crete near Salmone.
verses.27:8: And sailing alongside it with difficulty, we came to a certain place that is called Good Harbors, near which was the city of Thalassa.
verses.27:9: Now when much time had elapsed, and since sailing was no longer safe because even the Fast had already passed, Paul was consoling them,
verses.27:10: saying to them, "Men, I see that the voyage is going to be with harm and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives."
verses.27:11: But the centurion believed the helmsman and the shipowner more than the things that were being spoken by Paul.
verses.27:12: And since the harbor was not suitable for wintering, the majority decided on a plan to sail from there, if somehow they could arrive at and winter in Phoenix, a harbor of Crete facing toward the southwest and toward the northwest.
verses.27:13: And when a south wind blew gently, supposing that they had secured their purpose, after they had weighed anchor from Asson, they coasted along Crete.
verses.27:14: Not long afterward, however, a tempestuous wind, which is called Euroaquilo, hurled itself against it.
verses.27:15: And when the ship was seized and could not press into the wind, having given the ship over to the gusts, we were driven along.
verses.27:16: And running down toward a certain island that is called Cauda, we were able with difficulty to secure the skiff.
verses.27:17: When it had been hoisted up, they used supports, girding the ship; and fearing that they might run into the Syrtis, having lowered the gear, they were driven along in this way.
verses.27:18: And as we were tossed by a violent storm, on the following day they jettisoned cargo.
verses.27:19: And on the third day, with their own hands, they threw out the tackle of the ship.
verses.27:20: And with neither sun nor stars appearing for many days, and no small storm bearing down, all hope of our deliverance was now taken away.
verses.27:21: And when there had been much fasting, then Paul, standing in the midst of them, said, "Men, you indeed ought to have listened to me, not to have weighed anchor from Crete, and to have spared yourselves this harm and loss.
verses.27:22: And now I advise you to be of good courage, for there will be the loss of not a single life from among you, except of the ship.
verses.27:23: For an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me this night,
verses.27:24: saying, 'Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar; and look, God has granted to you all who are sailing with you.'
verses.27:25: For this reason, be of good courage, men; for I believe God that it will be just as it has been told to me.
verses.27:26: However, we must arrive at a certain island."
verses.27:27: But after the fourteenth night had come, as we were sailing in the Adriatic about midnight, the sailors suspected that some region was appearing to them.
verses.27:28: And they, letting down the sounding lead, found twenty fathoms; and after moving a little distance from there, they found fifteen fathoms.
verses.27:29: And fearing that we might run onto rough places, casting four anchors from the stern, they wished for day to come.
verses.27:30: But as the sailors were seeking to flee from the ship, after they had lowered the skiff into the sea under the pretext as if they were about to lay out anchors from the bow,
verses.27:31: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, "Unless these men remain in the ship, you cannot be saved."
verses.27:32: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the skiff and let it fall away.
verses.27:33: And as daylight was beginning to come, Paul was urging all of them to take food, saying, "Today, the fourteenth day, you remain waiting and fasting, taking nothing.
verses.27:34: For this reason I urge you to take food for your preservation; for not a hair from the head of any of you will perish."
verses.27:35: And when he had said these things, taking bread, he gave thanks to God in the sight of all; and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
verses.27:36: And having all become more encouraged, they themselves also took food.
verses.27:37: Now in all we were two hundred seventy-six souls in the ship.
verses.27:38: And when they were satisfied with food, they lightened the ship, throwing the wheat into the sea.
verses.27:39: And when day had come, they did not recognize the land; but they observed a certain bay having a beach, into which they planned, if they could, to drive the ship.
verses.27:40: And after they had weighed the anchors, they committed themselves to the sea, at the same time loosening the fastenings of the rudders; and having hoisted the foresail to the blowing of the breeze, they headed toward the beach.
verses.27:41: And when we had run onto a place between two seas, they drove the ship aground; and the bow, stuck fast, remained immovable, while the stern was being broken up by the force of the sea.
verses.27:42: Now the plan of the soldiers was to kill the prisoners, so that no one might swim away and escape.
verses.27:43: But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, prevented it from being done; and he commanded those who could swim to cast themselves out first, and to escape, and to come out onto the land.
verses.27:44: And the rest, some they carried on planks, and some upon the things that were from the ship. And so it came about that all the souls escaped to the land.
verses.28:1: And when we had escaped, we then learned that the island was called Malta. Now the native inhabitants showed us no ordinary kindness.
verses.28:2: For after lighting a fire, they refreshed all of us because of the threatening rain and the cold.
verses.28:3: Now when Paul had gathered a sizable quantity of brushwood and placed it on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and seized his hand.
verses.28:4: When the native inhabitants saw the creature hanging from his hand, they began saying to one another, "Surely this man is a murderer; though he has escaped from the sea, vengeance does not allow him to live."
verses.28:5: And he, shaking the creature off into the fire, suffered no harm.
verses.28:6: But they were expecting him to swell up and suddenly fall down and die. However, after waiting a long time and seeing no harm happening to him, they changed their minds and began saying that he was a god.
verses.28:7: Now in those parts were the estates of the leading man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and hosted us kindly for three days.
verses.28:8: And it happened that the father of Publius lay afflicted with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, and when he had prayed and laid hands on him, he healed him.
verses.28:9: When this had happened, all on the island who had illnesses kept coming and were cured.
verses.28:10: They also honored us with many honors, and as we set sail, they put on board for us the things that were necessary.
verses.28:11: After three months, we set sail on an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island, whose figurehead was Castor and Pollux.
verses.28:12: And when we had come to Syracuse, we stayed there for three days.
verses.28:13: From there, coasting along, we reached Rhegium; and after one day, with a south wind blowing, on the second day we came to Puteoli,
verses.28:14: where, having found brothers, we were asked to stay with them seven days; and so we came to Rome.
verses.28:15: And when the brothers from there had heard, they came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, giving thanks to God, he took courage.
verses.28:16: Now when we had come to Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.
verses.28:17: After the third day, however, he called together the foremost men of the Jews. And when they had gathered together, he said to them, "Men, brothers, having done nothing against the people or ancestral custom, I was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
verses.28:18: who, when they had held an examination of me, wanted to release me, because there was no basis for death in me.
verses.28:19: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not as though I had anything of which to accuse my nation.
verses.28:20: For this reason, therefore, I have asked to see you and to speak with you. For on account of the hope of Israel, I am bound with this chain."
verses.28:21: But they said to him, "We have neither received letters concerning you from Judea, nor has any of the brothers coming here reported or spoken anything evil about you.
verses.28:22: However, we ask to hear from you what you think; for concerning this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere."
verses.28:23: When they had appointed a day for him, very many came to him at his lodging; to them he expounded, bearing witness to the kingdom of God and seeking to persuade them concerning Jesus from the law of Moses and the prophets, from morning until evening.
verses.28:24: And some believed the things that were being said, while others did not believe.
verses.28:25: And since they were not in agreement with one another, they began to depart as Paul spoke one word: "The Holy Spirit spoke well through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
verses.28:26: saying, 'Go to this people and say to them, "You will hear with the ear and not understand, and seeing, you will see and not discern."
verses.28:27: For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have heard with difficulty, and they have pressed their eyes shut; otherwise they might see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back, and I would heal them.'
verses.28:28: Let it be known to you, therefore, that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they themselves will listen."
verses.28:30: Now he stayed for two full years in his own rented quarters, and he welcomed all who came in to him,
verses.28:31: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without restriction.

notes.1:4: Latin convescens translates Greek synalizomenos specifically as "eating with them" (rather than "staying/gathering with them"), and the Vulgate explicitly includes inquit ("He said") and per os meum ("through My mouth"), whereas the Greek has simply "which you heard from me."
notes.1:8: Latin virtutem supervenientis Spiritus Sancti in vos renders the Greek genitive absolute ("power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you") as a genitive phrase modifying "power" ("the power of the Holy Spirit coming upon you").
notes.1:16: The Clementine Vulgate uses the present tense oportet ("it is necessary"), whereas the Greek has the imperfect edei ("it was necessary" / "had to be").
notes.1:18: The Vulgate translates Greek prenes genomenos ("falling headlong") as suspensus ("being hanged" / "suspended"), harmonizing the passage with Judas hanging himself in Matthew 27:5.
notes.1:20: The Clementine Vulgate reads the plural eorum ("their dwelling"), agreeing with Psalm 68:26 (69:25), where the Greek text of Acts has the singular autou ("his"); Latin episcopatum literally denotes a "bishopric" or "office of oversight."
notes.2:23: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'affligentes' ("afflicting") rather than 'affigentes' ("fastening/nailing"), differing from the Greek 'prospexantes' ("having nailed [to a cross]").
notes.2:24: The Vulgate reads 'doloribus inferni' ("pains of the underworld," where Latin 'infernus' denotes the realm of the dead), differing from the Greek text's "pangs of death."
notes.2:33: The Vulgate reads masculine 'hunc, quem' ("this One, whom"), agreeing with the masculine noun Spiritus, whereas the Greek text uses the neuter "this which."
notes.2:42: The Vulgate links 'communicatione' with the genitive 'fractionis' ("the communion of the breaking of bread"), combining two terms that appear as separate coordinate nouns ("fellowship" and "the breaking of bread") in Greek.
notes.2:43: The Vulgate includes 'in Jerusalem' ("in Jerusalem") and the closing clause 'et metus erat magnus in universis' ("and there was great dread among all of them"), phrases absent from standard Greek editions.
notes.3:6: The Vulgate reads surge, et ambula ("rise and walk"), aligning with the Byzantine Greek tradition rather than the shorter Alexandrian Greek reading ("walk").
notes.3:7: The Vulgate translates the healed parts as bases ejus et plantae ("his feet and soles"), whereas the Greek text reads "feet and ankles."
notes.3:12: The Clementine Vulgate reads virtute aut potestate ("power or authority"), in contrast to the Greek text's "power or piety."
notes.3:13: Here and in 3:26, the Vulgate renders the Greek title pais ("servant/child") as filius ("Son").
notes.3:20: The Vulgate literally reproduces ut cum ("so that when") and reads qui praedicatus est ("who has been preached"), differing from the Alexandrian Greek reading "who has been appointed."
notes.4:4: The Vulgate gives the figure quinque millia ("five thousand") without the Greek qualifier "about."
notes.4:10: The Clementine Vulgate includes Domini nostri ("our Lord") before "Jesus Christ the Nazarene," an addition not found in the standard Greek text.
notes.4:12: The Latin salus ("salvation") and salvos fieri ("be saved") share the root of salvus factus est ("has been made well") in 4:9.
notes.4:21: The Vulgate reads clarificabant id quod factum fuerat in eo quod acciderat ("were glorifying what had been done in that which had happened"), without "God," whereas the Greek reads "were glorifying God for what had happened."
notes.4:27: Here the Vulgate translates Greek pais as puerum ("Servant," matching David pueri tui in 4:25), whereas in 4:30 it translates the same Greek title for Jesus as filii ("Son").
notes.5:3: Vulgate reads "tentavit" ("tempted"), where the Greek text has "eplērōsen" ("filled").
notes.5:6: Vulgate reads "amoverunt eum" ("removed him"), differing from the Greek "synesteilan auton" ("wrapped him up").
notes.5:15: The final clause "et liberarentur ab infirmitatibus suis" ("and they might be freed from their infirmities") is a distinctive Western and Clementine Vulgate reading not found in the standard Greek text.
notes.5:22: Vulgate includes the ablative absolute "aperto carcere" ("after the prison was opened"), where the Greek reads simply "did not find them in the prison."
notes.5:39: Vulgate reads neuter singular "illud" ("it," referring to the plan or work), whereas the Greek has masculine plural "autous" ("them," referring to the apostles).
notes.6:1: Vulgate renders Greek "Hellēnistōn" (Greek-speaking Jews) literally as "Græcorum" ("of the Greeks") and uses the stronger verb "despicerentur" ("were being slighted" or "looked down upon") for Greek "paretheōrounto" ("were being overlooked").
notes.6:5: Vulgate renders Greek "prosēlyton" with "advenam" (lit. "newcomer" or "stranger"); elsewhere it keeps the loanword proselytus (e.g. 2:11).
notes.6:7: Vulgate reads "verbum Domini" ("the word of the Lord"), where the Greek text reads "ho logos tou theou" ("the word of God").
notes.6:10: Vulgate reads nominative "qui loquebatur" ("the Spirit who was speaking"), making the Spirit the grammatical subject, whereas the Greek reads dative "hō elalei" ("the Spirit by which he [Stephen] was speaking").
notes.7:6: The Clementine Vulgate reads ei ("to him") where the Greek text has houtos ("thus"), introducing indirect discourse with Quia ("that") before shifting to direct speech in 7:7.
notes.7:7: The Clementine Vulgate reads Dominus ("the Lord") where the Greek text reads ho theos ("God").
notes.7:16: The Clementine Vulgate distinctly reads filii Sichem ("the son of Shechem"), whereas the Greek has tou en Sychem ("in Shechem," or in some manuscripts tou Sychem), and Genesis 33:19 calls Hamor the father of Shechem.
notes.7:30: The Clementine Vulgate reads in igne flammae rubi ("in the fire of a flame of a bush"), reversing the Greek noun order ("in a flame of fire of a bush").
notes.7:38: The Clementine Vulgate reads verba vitae ("words of life") where the Greek text has logia zonta ("living oracles").
notes.7:43: The Clementine Vulgate preserves the spelling Rempham for this deity's name, whereas critical Greek editions read Rephan (Rhaiphan).
notes.7:45: Latin Jesu here (like Greek Iesou) refers to Joshua, son of Nun, and is rendered with the standard English spelling "Joshua."
notes.7:55: In Clementine Vulgate versification, 7:55 includes Stephen's exclamation ("And he said..."), which modern editions number separately as 7:56.
notes.7:60: The Clementine Vulgate distinctly adds in Domino ("in the Lord") after obdormivit ("he fell asleep"), and includes the closing sentence about Saul, which modern editions place at 8:1a.
notes.8:5: The Clementine Vulgate prints the third-person plural verb praedicabant ("were proclaiming") with the singular subject Philippus ("Philip"), an unusual textual reading likely arising as a scribal or printing slip for singular praedicabat (or understood loosely of Philip and those with him).
notes.8:7: The Latin literally makes "many of those who had unclean spirits" (Multi eorum...) the grammatical subject of "came out" (exibant), reproducing a grammatical shift (anacoluthon) also found in some Greek manuscripts; in meaning, it is the unclean spirits that cried out and came out of those afflicted.
notes.8:12: Unlike the Greek text, which links "and the name of Jesus Christ" to Philip's preaching, the Clementine Vulgate attaches in nomine Jesu Christi ("in the name of Jesus Christ") directly to baptizabantur ("were being baptized").
notes.8:22: Where the Greek reads "the Lord," the Clementine Vulgate reads Deum ("God"); poenitentiam ... age is the standard Latin idiom for "repent."
notes.8:33: Where the Greek uses present-tense verbs in this Isaiah quotation, the Vulgate renders non aperuit in verse 32 in the past tense ("did not open") and tolletur in verse 33 in the future passive ("will be taken away").
notes.9:5: The Vulgate includes the clause "it is hard for you to kick against the goad" (with singular Latin "stimulum"), which is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts here and appears instead in Acts 26:14.
notes.9:6: In the Latin text this sentence begins verse 7.
notes.9:7: Latin "stabant stupefacti" means "stood astounded" rather than the Greek "stood speechless."
notes.9:12: The Clementine Vulgate encloses this verse in parentheses and omits "in a vision" (found in many Greek manuscripts). The present subjunctive "recipiat" (primary sequence) suits reading "vidit" as "has seen," continuing the Lord's speech.
notes.9:29: Where the Greek text names a single group ("the Hellenists"), the Vulgate uniquely distinguishes two groups: "speaking to the Gentiles" ("gentibus") and "disputing with the Greeks" ("Græcis").
notes.9:31: The Vulgate reads "replebatur" ("was being filled") with the consolation of the Holy Spirit, whereas the Greek text reads "was multiplied" or "increased."
notes.10:6: The Clementine Vulgate includes the closing clause "he will tell you what you must do" (hic dicet tibi quid te oporteat facere), which is absent from critical Greek editions.
notes.10:28: The Vulgate reads "abominable" (abominatum) rather than "unlawful" (Greek athemiton), expressing the strong ritual repulsion toward associating with a foreigner.
notes.10:33: The Clementine Vulgate reads "in your sight" (in conspectu tuo, referring to Peter), whereas most Greek manuscripts read "before God."
notes.10:45: The Vulgate reads "the grace of the Holy Spirit" (gratia Spiritus Sancti), whereas the Greek text reads "the gift of the Holy Spirit."
notes.10:48: The Clementine Vulgate preserves the full title "in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ" (in nomine Domini Jesu Christi), whereas critical Greek editions read "in the name of Jesus Christ" and the Byzantine tradition reads "in the name of the Lord."
notes.11:3: Latin Quare introisti ("Why did you go in") frames the charge as a question, whereas the critical Greek text has a statement ("You went in"). "Men who are uncircumcised" translates the blunt Latin phrase viros praeputium habentes (literally, "men having a foreskin").
notes.11:11: The Clementine Vulgate reads in qua eram ("in which I was"), following the first-person singular Greek variant where the critical Greek text reads "in which we were."
notes.11:17: Latin eamdem gratiam ("the same grace") renders the Greek phrase meaning "the same gift."
notes.11:19: Latin sub Stephano (literally "under Stephen," meaning "at the time of Stephen") renders the Greek circumstantial phrase epi Stephano ("over" or "because of Stephen").
notes.11:20: The Vulgate reads ad Graecos ("to the Greeks"), aligning with Greek manuscripts reading Hellenas rather than Hellenistas ("Hellenists").
notes.12:5: Latin sine intermissione ("without ceasing") differs in nuance from the Greek ektenos ("earnestly" or "fervently").
notes.12:19: Latin jussit eos duci ("he ordered them to be led away") preserves the concise idiom for being led off to execution.
notes.12:20: Latin ab illo ("by him") refers directly to Herod, whereas the Greek apo tes basilikes means "from the king's country."
notes.12:22: The Clementine Vulgate reads the plural Dei voces ("The voices of a god"), whereas the Greek has the singular "the voice of a god."
notes.12:25: The Clementine Vulgate reads ab Jerosolymis ("from Jerusalem"), whereas many modern critical editions of the Greek text read "to Jerusalem."
notes.13:1: The Vulgate reads Simon rather than the Greek form Symeon found in modern critical editions.
notes.13:20: Following the Vulgate wording (quasi post quadringentos et quinquaginta annos: et post hæc dedit judices), the four hundred and fifty years precede the period of the judges, whereas modern Greek critical editions attach the duration to the judges themselves.
notes.13:30: The Vulgate explicitly adds tertia die ("on the third day"), a reading absent from the standard Greek text, and includes the clause "and He was seen for many days by those" at the end of verse 30 rather than verse 31.
notes.13:36: The Clementine Vulgate punctuates after administrasset, joining voluntati Dei with dormivit ("fell asleep by the will of God"); the dative voluntati Dei can also be construed with administrasset ("when he had served the will of God in his own generation").
notes.13:48: The Vulgate renders the Greek participle tetagmenoi ("appointed" or "disposed") with the specific compound præordinati ("preordained").
notes.14:3: The Vulgate reads fiducialiter agentes ("acting boldly/confidently"), whereas the Greek has παρρησιαζόμενοι ("speaking boldly").
notes.14:6: The Clementine Vulgate includes the closing clause et ibi evangelizantes erant ("and there they were preaching the gospel") inside verse 6, so there is no separate verse 7.
notes.14:12: Here and in verse 13, the Vulgate renders the Greek deity names Zeus and Hermes with their Roman equivalents, Jupiter (Jovem/Jovis) and Mercury (Mercurium).
notes.14:15: The Vulgate renders the Greek adjective ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ("of like nature") with the fuller phrase mortales sumus, similes vobis homines ("we also are mortals, men like you").
notes.14:17: The Vulgate connects de cælo ("from heaven") to benefaciens ("doing good") and reads corda nostra ("our hearts") rather than "your hearts".
notes.15:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads quidam alii ex aliis ("certain others from among the others" or "from the other side") rather than ex illis ("from among them"), and has only seditione ("dissension") without a second noun for "debate".
notes.15:14: The Vulgate uses the standard form Simon where the Greek text uses the Semitic form Symeon.
notes.15:18: The Vulgate reads this as a complete sentence with singular opus suum ("His work"), differing from both the shorter critical Greek text attached to verse 17 and the Byzantine plural ("all His works").
notes.15:33: Verse 34 (Silas's decision to remain in Antioch) is present in this Latin text and is shown as an additional verse after 15:33, since the Saints numbering has no slot for it.
notes.15:41: The closing clause præcipiens custodire præcepta Apostolorum et seniorum ("commanding them to keep the precepts of the apostles and the elders") is a distinctive Western/Vulgate expansion absent from standard Greek editions; in verse 40 the Vulgate also reads gratiæ Dei ("grace of God") rather than "grace of the Lord".
notes.16:1: Here and in verse 3 the Vulgate renders the Greek term for "Greek" as "gentilis" ("Gentile").
notes.16:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads the future tense "abundabunt" ("will abound"), whereas the Greek text and some Latin witnesses read the imperfect ("were increasing/abounding").
notes.16:12: The Vulgate renders the Greek participle for "staying" as "conferentes" ("conferring" or "conversing"), highlighting discussion during their stay in Philippi.
notes.16:16: Latin "spiritum pythonem" preserves the Greek reference to a divining spirit associated with the Pythian oracle of Apollo at Delphi.
notes.16:38: In the Clementine Vulgate, Paul's closing clause begins verse 38 rather than ending verse 37, and repeats the verb "ejicio" ("cast out") from verse 37 rather than shifting to "bring out" as in the Greek.
notes.17:4: The Vulgate reads de colentibus gentilibusque ("of the worshipers and Gentiles"), coordinating two groups with -que and reading "Gentiles" rather than the Greek "devout Greeks."
notes.17:6: The Clementine Vulgate reads urbem ("the city") rather than orbem ("the world," corresponding to Greek oikoumenen).
